title: Project Sceptrum - Multilingual AI Coding Evaluation Specialist - Dutch
description: Join a short, paid project that tests whether AI coding agents work as well on instructions written in the target language as they do in English. Your language skills and technical background decide where you fit. About the project Welo Data is helping evaluate how well AI coding agents perform when the instructions they receive are written in languages other than English. Agents are given a real software engineering task in a code repository, and automated tests check whether they solved it. The code, repositories and tests stay exactly as they are. Only the human-written instructions change language, so the quality of every instruction directly affects the result. About the roles There are two roles on this project. We place you in one of them based on your experience & skillsets. Translator: translate English software engineering task briefs into the target language. You keep every requirement, constraint and success condition, and you leave commands, file paths, API names, code and test conditions exactly as written in English. This role suits people with a stronger technical background, and translation experience is a plus. Reviewer: compare each translation with the English source, check that nothing is missing, added or changed in meaning, correct errors, and log each correction by error type. This role suits people with strong translation, editing or review experience and enough technical familiarity to read code context. Who we are looking for Native or near-native writing in the target language, and strong reading ability in English. Either professional experience in translation, editing, review or technical writing, or a software background combined with excellent writing in the target language Comfort reading technical text. Coding experience is a strong plus for the translation role and helpful for the review role. Close attention to detail. In this project, a dropped clause can make a task fail. Project at a glance Project duration: one week since the mid of November Languages: Dutch Project time commitment: 6 hours per person Project compensation: varies depends on different programming language Work location: fully remote How selection works (major steps) Screening questions: about 2 minutes. They cover your language background, translation and review experience, which programming languages you know and how well, and your availability. Language test: short exercises in the target language. Programming skills assessment: you will be invited to another opportunity, in the programming language you know best (Rust, Go, Python, or TypeScript / JavaScript). It confirms your technical level and places you in a language track. Financial Onboarding & Role placement: complete the financial onboarding with Welo Data. In the meanwhile, you will be informed about the decision whether you are placed in the initial translation role or the review role. Production: once you finish all steps above, our project team will contact you for production. Job Reference: #L1-CC1 Compensation Additional Information Why Join Welo Data? ✨ Limitless Flexibility Project-based opportunities that fit your availability. Choose when and how much you want to contribute—fully remote, with complete autonomy. 🌱 Limitless Growth Optional access to AI and Large Language Model workshops designed specifically for professionals like you. No coding required—just your expertise. 🌍 Limitless Support Be part of a global contributor community with responsive guidance and support. 💡 Real Impact Apply your expertise in the Legal field to influence the AI systems shaping the future of your industry—while collaborating with data professionals and expanding your skills. How to Apply? Apply now by answering a few quick questions to join our database and become part of our growing community. About Welo Data Welo Data, part of Welocalize, is a global AI data company with 500,000+ contributors delivering high-quality, ethical data to train the world’s most advanced AI systems. We’re building smarter, more human AI with a diverse community in 100+ countries. At Welo Data, Limitless AI. Limitless You. isn’t just a slogan—it’s our promise. We build smarter AI through the power of human contribution, offering limitless opportunities for our global community to grow, contribute, and work on their terms.

title: Senior Full Stack Engineer - Databases - Analytics | UK | Remote
description: Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X . We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do. You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity. This is a remote opportunity, and we would be interested in applicants located in Spain, Sweden, UK, Ireland or Germany. The Opportunity: At Grafana Labs, we build observability tools that help users understand, respond to, and improve their systems – regardless of scale, complexity, or tech stack. We recently started a skunkworks initiative with a mission to bring observability to the rest of the business. Our goal is to make Grafana the single best place where humans and AI agents understand and act on real-time data from across the enterprise. As part of this initiative, we are building an AI-native data intelligence system that gives agents reliable, governed access to enterprise context. This system helps agents retrieve the right data, metadata, definitions, lineage, quality signals, and institutional knowledge without every agent builder having to maintain their own brittle context files. The principle is simple: the context system retrieves, agents decide, and data teams maintain the intelligence. The new team is a mix of seasoned Grafanistas and new hires. We operate with a high degree of autonomy and ownership, both as individuals and as a team. Engineers are empowered to make decisions, move quickly, and validate ideas early – while being supported by a deeply collaborative culture that values curiosity, feedback, and cross-functional partnership. We’re looking for a Staff-level Backend Engineer to help build the first production services for this context layer management system. You will design and ship the core backend architecture that powers ingestion, context storage, retrieval APIs, and agent-facing integrations. This is an early-stage role on a high-autonomy team, so you should be comfortable working through ambiguity, making pragmatic architectural decisions, and building systems that can evolve from internal dogfooding to production-grade SaaS. As the team matures, there’s a broad opportunity to expand or redefine this role based on impact and initiative. What You'll Be Doing: Build the core backend services: Design, implement, test, and operate the first services for context ingestion, context indexing, retrieval orchestration, API access, source configuration, and system administration. Create a scalable SaaS foundation: Help define and build the architecture for a multi-tenant service, including tenant isolation, usage tracking, quotas, audit logs, background jobs, and reliable service boundaries. Power agent-facing retrieval workflows: Build APIs and service interfaces that allow AI agents, MCP tools, CLIs, and internal applications to retrieve relevant context, provenance, confidence signals, and warnings. Work across product and infrastructure: Partner with the team to make practical tradeoffs between fast experimentation and long-term reliability, especially as the project moves from prototype to production. Operate what you build: Instrument services with metrics, logs, traces, alerts, and dashboards. Use observability tools to understand system behavior and improve reliability. Contribute to technical direction: Help shape the architecture, service boundaries, storage choices, API contracts, deployment patterns, and engineering practices for a new product area. Effective communication: You’ll be working in a highly dynamic and collaborative environment, so we need someone who can communicate effectively and contribute across teams. Ownership and impact: Take full ownership of the AI solutions you develop, ensuring they are not only innovative but also scalable, maintainable, and aligned with real user workflows. What Makes You a Great Fit: Strong engineering skills: Solid experience building production-grade, user-facing software systems. You’re a self-starter, capable of tackling complex engineering problems and making UI design decisions with minimal supervision. AI experience with a practical mindset: You’re familiar with AI technologies and frameworks, and you focus on delivering high-quality solutions that work in the real world, not just in theory. Quick iteration and experimentation: You’re comfortable releasing prototypes, collecting feedback, and iterating with a pragmatic mindset. Proven initiative: You take ownership and drive projects forward, pushing boundaries to find the most impactful solutions. You can deal with ambiguity and are able to define scope where things are loosely defined. Collaborative attitude: You communicate effectively with your peers. You’re open to feedback, and you bring a solutions-oriented mindset to the table. Experience with LLMs, prompt engineering, and building applications powered by GenAI. Proven track record of delivering software that made it into production and is actively used by users. Exposure to working in cloud-native environments (e.g., AWS, GCP, Azure). Experience using observability tools to understand and troubleshoot system behavior. Bonus Points for: Experience building or working with agent frameworks or multi‑agent workflows. Experience as a data analyst or work with data platforms (e.g., Looker, Tableau, PowerBI, Snowflake, DataBricks) Experience building tools for data engineering. How we work: We are a remote-first team that meets regularly over video and does most of our work asynchronously, in writing. We value creativity, diverse perspectives, and clear communication. Tempo is relied upon by prominent global organizations to monitor critical applications and infrastructure, and we expect everyone on the team, including our Staff engineers, to contribute ideas that make it a more reliable, more useful, and more loved product. Compensation & Rewards: In the United Kingdom, the Base compensation range for this role is GBP 103,958 - GBP 124,750. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed in the interview process. Benefits include equity, bonus (if applicable) and other benefits listed here . *Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process *Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process. Why You’ll Thrive at Grafana Labs: 100% Remote, Global Culture - As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose. Scaling Organization – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment. Transparent Communication – Expect open decision-making and regular company-wide updates. Innovation-Driven – Autonomy and support to ship great work and try new things. Open Source Roots – Built on community-driven values that shape how we work. Empowered Teams – High trust, low ego culture that values outcomes over optics. Career Growth Pathways – Defined opportunities to grow and develop your career. Approachable Leadership – Transparent execs who are involved, visible, and human. Passionate People – Join a team of smart, supportive folks who care deeply about what they do. In-Person onboarding - We want you to thrive from day 1 with your fellow new ‘Grafanistas’ to learn all about what we do and how we do it. Balance is Key - We operate a global annual leave policy of 30 days per annum. 3 days of your annual leave entitlement are reserved for Grafana Shutdown Days to allow the team to really disconnect. *We will comply with local legislation where applicable. Equal Opportunity Employer: Grafana Labs is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from everyone regardless of race, colour, nationality, origin, caste, sex, gender reassignment identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, religion or belief, disability, veteran status, genetic information, pregnancy, maternity, marital, family or carer status, or any other characteristic which is protected by local law. We believe that equality and diversity build a strong organisation, and we work hard to ensure that is the foundation of our organisation as we grow. title: Italian Multimedia Content Reviewer
description: About Welocalize Welocalize, a Welo Global brand, serves localization teams through AI-enabled multilingual content solutions that enable enterprises to operate and scale globally. Welocalize combines AI, automation, and human expertise to support enterprises in more than 300 languages, enabling accurate, culturally aligned, and compliant multilingual content at scale. Welocalize’s Opal Platform comprises patented technology designed to automate multilingual content and improve workflow performance for enterprises. Opal functions as an agentic system that orchestrates AI, automation, and human expertise to coordinate content workflows across the lifecycle, improving speed, scalability, and operational control for global enterprises. These solutions operate within a secure and compliant environment supported by seven ISO certifications. Welocalize is headquartered in New York with offices worldwide. welocalize.com Job Description Summary In this exciting position, the Multimedia Content Reviewer will be responsible for writing, adapting, reviewing, and evaluating a wide range of linguistic and multimedia content in Italian, ensuring the highest standards of linguistic accuracy, cultural relevance, and overall quality for customers using the world's foremost multimedia platforms. The role combines creative and editorial expertise with analytical and quality evaluation skills, covering traditional localization work as well as emerging content types, including AI-generated content, linguistic annotation, and structured content evaluations. With time, the Multimedia Content Reviewer will become the cultural ambassador for their language market and will be expected to produce fully localized content, flag potential cultural issues, and articulate suggestions to make all content appropriate and relevant for the target market. The ideal candidate possesses a background in journalism, editorial content, copywriting, or a related field, has proven creative writing skills, and a keen attention to detail. They should also demonstrate strong critical thinking, sound editorial judgment, and the flexibility to navigate different workflows, guidelines, and content evaluation methodologies. In addition, we're seeking candidates who are passionate about music, film, sports, gaming, and technology, and have a knack for iOS and macOS devices. Main Duties Localize, translate, and adapt content of various categories (i.e. multimedia, legal, technical, marketing, sports, entertainment, health and wellness, and other digital content) while adhering to writing style guides and project-specific guidelines. Write new copy for a range of multimedia products such as music, TV, film, sports, apps, video on-demand, game subscription services, and more. Copy-edit and fact-check content to ensure accuracy, clarity, consistency, and cultural relevance. Perform LQA (Localization QA) testing of content published on live platforms (music and app descriptions, marketing material, and marketing campaigns). Evaluate human-written and AI-generated content for linguistic accuracy, fluency, relevance, consistency, and adherence to project-specific quality standards. Perform linguistic annotation, content classification, and structured evaluation tasks using predefined guidelines, rating scales, and quality criteria. Identify and document errors, inconsistencies, and quality issues, providing clear, actionable feedback and supporting rationale for evaluation decisions. Conduct market-specific research on local content treatment, audience preferences, cultural nuances, product and terminology trends, and best localization practices for the target audience. Report on data and/or assets across a broad scope of media and content types, ensuring accuracy, consistency, and compliance with project requirements. Collaborate with global language teams via virtual meetings and email on content review tasks to align on terminology, style, quality standards, evaluation criteria, and market-specific insights. Requirements BS/BA and 2+ years of work experience in journalism, copywriting, editing, digital media, content production, or a related field. Experience in translation and localization of multimedia content or demonstrated experience adapting content for Brazilian audiences. Native-level proficiency in Brazilian Portuguese, with excellent grammar, writing, editing, and linguistic judgment skills. Ability to quickly detect issues and inconsistencies across large volumes of content and make sound judgment calls based on the information at hand. Ability to interpret and consistently apply detailed guidelines, rating scales, and evaluation frameworks across different projects. Familiarity with AI-generated content, linguistic annotation, content evaluation, or data quality assessment is a plus. Is in tune with and has a wide range of knowledge of music, film, TV, sports, gaming, technology, and Brazilian pop culture. Has the ability to own linguistic quality for the Brazilian Portuguese market and make confident linguistic decisions. Must be highly detail-oriented with the ability to multitask, prioritize, and meet deadlines. Fluency in written and verbal English. Strong computer literacy; knowledge of iOS/macOS systems is a plus. Ability to work independently and remotely. Collaborative; enjoys teamwork in a multicultural environment and is open to feedback, calibration, and continuous learning. Compensation Additional Information

title: Implementation Specialist
description: I quit medicine because I kept watching patients die needlessly, for avoidable reasons. In almost every case, the medical knowledge and clinicians were there. It was the system that failed: the way information moved, decisions got routed, and fragmented teams and data turned solvable problems into tragedy. I started Anima to change that. Our mission is human wellbeing, and we believe personalised medicine will transform it. Our founding insight is that getting there requires a system that learns continuously from care and its outcomes, optimising for human wellbeing. Building that learning engine is the opportunity at the heart of Anima. We're now in 1,000+ clinics across 5 product lines, serving more than 25% of the UK population. We are cash flow positive, growing fast, and have a tight crew of ~45 people who care deeply for each other and the mission. Everyone has real ownership and a voice in decisions. Multiple trillion-dollar companies will be built in healthcare over the next two decades. We intend to be one of them. If you want to work on problems where the stakes are high, you belong at Anima. Your work here will save lives. -- Shun £65k–£90k base, plus equity UK remote, UK working hours, with occasional UK customer visits The role Help GP practices make a confident start with Anima. Last quarter, we onboarded 131 practices. We’re building a dedicated Implementation team to support that growth, and you’ll be one of its first members. You’ll own each implementation from kick-off through go-live and early support, helping practice teams build the skills and confidence to use Anima independently. You’ll also help shape how we implement: improving workflows, developing training and building a playbook that works across hundreds of practices. What you’ll do Own implementations from start to finish. Coordinate kick-off, configuration and go-live, aiming to get most practices live within their first week. Make Anima work for each practice. Understand how their team operates and configure workflows around their needs. Teach people to use it confidently. Run clear, practical training for clinicians and practice teams, adapting your approach to different levels of technical confidence. Build confidence beyond go-live. Develop practice super users, provide 1–2 weeks of hypercare and hand over cleanly to Support and Customer Success. Make great implementation repeatable. Create reusable training and group webinars. Use feedback from customers, Support and CS to solve recurring problems at their source. What you’ll bring SaaS experience. You’ve worked directly with customers on a SaaS product in onboarding, implementation or training. Strong teaching and communication skills. You can make something unfamiliar feel manageable and check that people can put it into practice. Patience and adaptability. You respond thoughtfully when someone is struggling or their priorities change. Practical problem-solving. You learn products quickly and can work out why a workflow isn’t delivering the intended result. Ownership and organisation. You can keep several implementations moving while making the next steps clear to everyone involved. Healthcare experience isn’t required—we’ll help you learn primary care. Experience creating training videos, guides or webinars would be useful. What we offer Anima should be where you do your life’s best work. We support that with: Time off: 25 days’ annual leave plus 8 UK public holidays, with flexible additional time off. Health cover: private medical, dental, vision and mental health insurance. Parental leave: 12 weeks’ maternity leave at full pay, rising to 24 weeks after two years; 4 weeks’ paternity leave at full pay. Pension: 4% employer contributions, with salary sacrifice and 100% of the employer National Insurance savings passed on to you. Learning: £1,000 annual budget for your development. Fitness: gym subscription matching up to £50 per month. Equipment: a high-spec MacBook and a home office budget. Time together: two full-team off-sites each year, previous destinations include Mykonos and Mexico. Farringdon office: a beautiful new London HQ, with most of the team together at least twice a week. Everyone is welcome at Anima. We strongly believe in building a diverse and inclusive team. If you’re excited by our mission and believe you could do this work well, we’d love to hear from you, even if your experience doesn’t match every point above. If adjustments would help you participate fully in the interview process, please let us know.

title: English to German Austria Medical Devices Linguist
description: About Welo Life Sciences Welo Life Sciences, a Welo Global brand, is a specialized language and technology partner serving pharmaceutical, CRO, and medical device organizations operating in regulated global markets. We deliver regulator-ready translation, linguistic validation, and localization solutions that support clinical trials, pharmacovigilance, regulatory affairs, labeling, and global commercialization. Our approach combines subject matter expertise with ISO-certified quality processes and technology-enabled workflows designed to integrate seamlessly into life sciences operations. With extensive experience supporting global product development and post-market requirements, Welo Life Sciences helps organizations accelerate timelines, protect data integrity, and maintain compliance across languages and regions. All solutions are delivered within a secure, audit-ready framework supported by seven ISO certifications. welolifesciences.com About the Role We are looking for experienced English (UK) into German (Austria) linguists specializing in Medical Devices documentation translation and review. Key Responsibilities Translate medical device documentation from English (UK) into German (Austria). Perform Machine Translation Post-Editing (MTPE) on machine-translated medical content. Perform Copy Edit (translation review) of translated and post-edited content, ensuring accuracy, terminology consistency, and compliance with project-specific quality requirements. Fix linguistic issues identified during quality checks and client reviews. Address linguistic feedback and implement required corrections in accordance with project guidelines. Meet agreed deadlines and maintain consistent quality across assigned projects. Work within the client's CAT tool environment using XTM (license provided). Field of Expertise Medical Devices: Instructions for Use (IFUs), user manuals, operating instructions, product documentation, technical documentation, labelling and user interfaces. Medical and technical documentation related to medical devices, ensuring accurate terminology and compliance with industry-specific requirements. Must-Have Criteria Relevant Translation Experience At least two years of professional translation experience in Life Sciences, specifically involving Medical Devices and medical documentation. Practical experience translating and reviewing medical device-related documentation. Familiarity with ISO standards and quality requirements applicable to Life Sciences translation. Experience exclusively in Patents is not sufficient to meet the project requirements. Technical Skills Familiarity with CAT tools, particularly XTM. The client will provide an XTM license; there is no need to purchase one. Ability to perform Translation, Copy Edit, MTPE and linguistic issue correction tasks. Nice-to-Have Degree in Medicine, Biology, Biochemistry, Clinical Research, Translation, Linguistics, Philology or a related field. Previous experience working with medical device manufacturers, pharmaceutical companies, CROs or other Life Sciences organizations. Familiarity with medical terminology, regulatory requirements and quality assurance processes in the medical industry. Project Details Language Pair: English (UK) into German (Austria) Content Specialization: Medical Devices Task Types: Translation, Copy Edit, MTPE and Fix Linguistic Issues. Expected Capacity: Monthly. Expected Volume: Approximately 7,000 words per month. CAT Tool: XTM (license provided by the client). Before Applying Please note that an assessment will be part of our onboarding and quality procedure. Candidates will be required to complete the standard Medical Devices assessment. Please only apply if you are willing to complete the assessment. Please ensure your latest English CV accurately reflects your Life Sciences and Medical Devices translation experience, including: Total years of professional translation experience. Years of experience specifically in Medical Devices and In Vitro Diagnostics. Examples of medical documentation and content types translated. Your experience with memoQ (please specify the version used). Your experience performing both Translation and Copy Edit. Your contact information (email AND phone number). Beware of recruitment scams. Welo Global and all of its brands never recruit through direct messages on social media or WhatsApp, and never asks candidates to pay money for a job. title: Technical Program Manager - IP Backbone
description: About Nebius : Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure. Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI. Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D. The IP Backbone TPM coordinates the planning and delivery of Nebius’s global IP backbone and Internet edge. The role connects data center launches, customer and platform demand, IP architecture, network engineering, procurement, and external providers so that sites have the routing, transit, peering, hardware, and address resources needed for service readiness and growth. The TPM is accountable for end-to-end project coordination: defining scope with technical owners, building integrated plans, tracking dependencies and risks, driving decisions to closure, and confirming handover. Network Architecture and Engineering own technical standards and design decisions; engineers lead implementation. The TPM keeps those workstreams aligned and ensures the required outcomes are delivered. Nebius Regions and HQ In summer 2026, we introduced the concept of regions to remove dependence on the Amsterdam HQ and speed decision making. The regional change applies to procurement, logistics, and IT datacenter operations. Network infrastructure remains an HQ function because its architecture and design affect all sites. Position Scope Please note that Nebius is in a state of rapid growth. Due to this, the scope and responsibilities of the role will constantly evolve based on business and team needs. Site and PoP Readiness Coordinate IP connectivity due diligence for new data center and PoP locations. Confirm the planned site role in the backbone and the required connectivity to regional and Super PoPs. Track site dependencies such as rack space, power, security, cross-connects, cabling, hardware delivery, and carrier access. Coordinate PoP build plans with IP Engineering, Layer 1 Planning, Data Center Operations, , Security, and Procurement. Identify the boundary between IP and Layer 1 work early, including transport handoffs, demarcation points, and ownership of cross-connects. Confirm that IP equipment and provider services are ready for installation, testing, and operational handover. IP Connectivity Planning Coordinate plans for IP transit, peering, private interconnects, and backbone connectivity in line with the global network strategy. Track provider requirements, site availability, port capacity, cross-connects, delivery dates, commercial terms, and technical acceptance criteria. Work with Procurement and network architects to gather and review ISP information using the provider qualification checklist. Use the completed assessment and architect input to support provider selection and record the decision and any conditions. Plan connectivity for new data center launches, including the required paths from the front-end fabric to the Nebius backbone, transit providers, cloud on-ramps, and peering locations as applicable. Maintain an integrated view of circuit, port, router, optics, and cross-connect dependencies so that a delivered service can be activated end to end. Coordinate capacity growth and diverse connectivity plans before demand or a new launch creates a service constraint. Internet Routing Resources and Security Coordinate the lifecycle and accurate records for Nebius IPv4 and IPv6 address allocations, assignments, and utilization. Maintain an operational view of ASN use and dependencies across regions, PoPs, transit providers, peers, and customer-facing services. Coordinate the creation, review, and maintenance of AS-SETs, route objects, and ROAs with the responsible technical owners and relevant registries. Track RPKI and IRR readiness as part of provider onboarding, routing changes, and new-site launches. Coordinate remediation of resource or routing-security issues with Network Engineering and external providers. Backbone Hardware and Supply Maintain a forward-looking view of IP backbone hardware demand based on PoP builds, data center launches, capacity plans, and approved architecture. Coordinate hardware planning and delivery for routers, line cards, optics, spares, software entitlements, and related components. Standard platforms are Juniper MX304 routers for peering borders, Juniper PTX10002 routers for data center borders, and Cisco 8000 Series routers for Cloud Interconnect (CIC) and cloud on-ramps. Work with IP Engineering to translate approved designs into complete, validated bills of materials and deployment requirements. Track forecasts, purchase requests, supplier commitments, lead times, delivery allocations, and regional logistics with Network Supply and Procurement. Coordinate supply for PoP out-of-band equipment (currently MikroTik, with future SD-WAN platforms under consideration), console access, and PoP management networks. Security appliances are outside this role’s hardware scope. Identify supply risks early and coordinate mitigation options with technical owners, procurement, and project stakeholders. Keep project schedules aligned with hardware readiness, site readiness, and service activation milestones. Delivery and Launch Coordination Build and maintain integrated delivery plans for IP backbone projects, PoP builds, provider services, and data center launches. Coordinate work across IP Architecture, IP Engineering, Layer 1 Planning, Data Center Operations, Construction, Security, Procurement, and providers. Define milestones, prerequisites, owners, acceptance criteria, and handover requirements for each workstream. Drive resolution of blockers and escalate risks that could affect site launch, customer commitments, capacity, or network resilience. Coordinate testing, service activation, routing turn-up, documentation, and operational handover with the engineering and operations teams. Maintain clear status reporting for project scope, schedule, dependencies, decisions, risks, and actions. Operations and Capacity Management Track IP backbone and Internet edge capacity against forecast demand, data center growth, customer requirements, and platform launches. Coordinate port, router, transit, peering, address-resource, and hardware expansion before capacity constraints affect service readiness. Maintain accurate records of PoPs, providers, circuits, ports, ASNs, address allocations, AS-SETs, ROAs, and deployment status in the agreed systems of record. Support incident follow-up and provider escalations when delivery or service issues affect backbone availability. Review completed projects with technical and operations teams, capture lessons learned, and improve planning and handover processes. Support ongoing improvements to resiliency, routing security, provider diversity, and operational readiness. Working Boundaries with Layer 1 Planning IP and Layer 1 TPMs share delivery responsibility for PoP and data center connectivity projects. The IP TPM coordinates the IP service outcome: routing, transit, peering, IP address resources, IP hardware, and service activation. The Layer 1 TPM coordinates the physical and optical transport outcome: fiber routes, wavelengths or dark fiber, DWDM systems, ILAs, and the transport path to the agreed handoff. For shared projects, the two TPMs should maintain one integrated milestone plan, agree the service demarcation and handoff points with engineering, and assign a clear owner to each dependency. Technical design and configuration decisions remain with the relevant architecture and engineering owners. Internal Operating Context Nebius infrastructure supports Nebius Cloud Platform, Nebius Token Factory, Meta, Microsoft, and selected bare-metal customers. The IP backbone TPM works with product and infrastructure stakeholders to translate Nebius Cloud launches and requirements into deliverable connectivity plans. This scope covers Nebius Cloud by default; Internet access for a bare-metal customer is included when that customer specifically requests it. Cloud Interconnect requirements may require dedicated on-ramp planning. For provider onboarding, Procurement coordinates the commercial process and issues the qualification questionnaire. The TPM coordinates technical due diligence with Backbone Architecture and Engineering, tracks completion, and records the approval decision and follow-up actions. The TPM coordinates the provider assessment and selection process with Procurement and the network architects, using the qualification checklist and architect input to reach and document the decision. Security Project Coordination The TPM may coordinate IP security and DDoS-related projects that affect the backbone or Internet edge. Security Architects lead these projects and own the security architecture and technical decisions. The TPM coordinates scope, dependencies, milestones, risks, stakeholder communication, and delivery handover with Security, Network Architecture, Engineering, Procurement, and providers as needed. Key Collaborators Function Typical contribution IP / Backbone Architecture Defines architecture and technical standards; provides technical input to provider selection and design decisions IP Engineering Owns detailed design, configuration, implementation, testing, and technical handover Front End Fabric Deploy Team Ensures that OOB connectivity is ready, and that CAB + Border related deploy work is completed and unblocks this team. Layer 1 Planning / DWDM Engineering Delivers transport connectivity and coordinates shared PoP or site dependencies Network Supply and Procurement Forecasts and sources hardware and services; coordinates provider qualification and commercial processes Data Center Operations and Construction Delivers site access, space, power, cabling, cross-connect, and readiness dependencies Product and customer teams Provides launch dates, demand forecasts, and customer or platform requirements Security Architects Lead IP security and DDoS projects and own security architecture decisions ISPs, peers, exchanges, and cloud providers Deliver transit, peering, interconnection, and related services About Nebius Nebius AI is an AI cloud platform with one of the largest GPU capacities in Europe. Launched in November 2023, the Nebius AI platform provides high-end, training-optimized infrastructure for AI practitioners. As an NVIDIA preferred cloud service provider, Nebius AI offers a variety of NVIDIA GPUs for training and inference, as well as a set of tools for efficient multi-node training. Nebius AI owns a data center in Finland, built from the ground up by the company’s R&D team and showcasing our commitment to sustainability. The data center is home to ISEG, the most powerful commercially available supercomputer in Europe and the 16th most powerful globally (Top 500 list, November 2023). Nebius’s headquarters are in Amsterdam, Netherlands, with teams working out of R&D hubs across Europe and the Middle East. Nebius AI is built with the talent of more than 500 highly skilled engineers with a proven track record in developing sophisticated cloud and ML solutions and designing cutting-edge hardware. This allows all the layers of the Nebius AI cloud – from hardware to UI – to be built in-house, distictly differentiating Nebius AI from the majority of specialized clouds: Nebius customers get a true hyperscaler-cloud experience tailored for AI practitioners. title: Senior Full Stack Engineer - Databases, Analytics | Spain | Remote
description: Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X . We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do. You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity. This is a remote opportunity, and we would be interested in applicants located in Spain, Sweden, UK, Ireland or Germany. The Opportunity: At Grafana Labs, we build observability tools that help users understand, respond to, and improve their systems – regardless of scale, complexity, or tech stack. We recently started a skunkworks initiative with a mission to bring observability to the rest of the business. Our goal is to make Grafana the single best place where humans and AI agents understand and act on real-time data from across the enterprise. As part of this initiative, we are building an AI-native data intelligence system that gives agents reliable, governed access to enterprise context. This system helps agents retrieve the right data, metadata, definitions, lineage, quality signals, and institutional knowledge without every agent builder having to maintain their own brittle context files. The principle is simple: the context system retrieves, agents decide, and data teams maintain the intelligence. The new team is a mix of seasoned Grafanistas and new hires. We operate with a high degree of autonomy and ownership, both as individuals and as a team. Engineers are empowered to make decisions, move quickly, and validate ideas early – while being supported by a deeply collaborative culture that values curiosity, feedback, and cross-functional partnership. We’re looking for a Staff-level Backend Engineer to help build the first production services for this context layer management system. You will design and ship the core backend architecture that powers ingestion, context storage, retrieval APIs, and agent-facing integrations. This is an early-stage role on a high-autonomy team, so you should be comfortable working through ambiguity, making pragmatic architectural decisions, and building systems that can evolve from internal dogfooding to production-grade SaaS. As the team matures, there’s a broad opportunity to expand or redefine this role based on impact and initiative. What You'll Be Doing: Build the core backend services: Design, implement, test, and operate the first services for context ingestion, context indexing, retrieval orchestration, API access, source configuration, and system administration. Create a scalable SaaS foundation: Help define and build the architecture for a multi-tenant service, including tenant isolation, usage tracking, quotas, audit logs, background jobs, and reliable service boundaries. Power agent-facing retrieval workflows: Build APIs and service interfaces that allow AI agents, MCP tools, CLIs, and internal applications to retrieve relevant context, provenance, confidence signals, and warnings. Work across product and infrastructure: Partner with the team to make practical tradeoffs between fast experimentation and long-term reliability, especially as the project moves from prototype to production. Operate what you build: Instrument services with metrics, logs, traces, alerts, and dashboards. Use observability tools to understand system behavior and improve reliability. Contribute to technical direction: Help shape the architecture, service boundaries, storage choices, API contracts, deployment patterns, and engineering practices for a new product area. Effective communication: You’ll be working in a highly dynamic and collaborative environment, so we need someone who can communicate effectively and contribute across teams. Ownership and impact: Take full ownership of the AI solutions you develop, ensuring they are not only innovative but also scalable, maintainable, and aligned with real user workflows. What Makes You a Great Fit: Strong engineering skills: Solid experience building production-grade, user-facing software systems. You’re a self-starter, capable of tackling complex engineering problems and making UI design decisions with minimal supervision. AI experience with a practical mindset: You’re familiar with AI technologies and frameworks, and you focus on delivering high-quality solutions that work in the real world, not just in theory. Quick iteration and experimentation: You’re comfortable releasing prototypes, collecting feedback, and iterating with a pragmatic mindset. Proven initiative: You take ownership and drive projects forward, pushing boundaries to find the most impactful solutions. You can deal with ambiguity and are able to define scope where things are loosely defined. Collaborative attitude: You communicate effectively with your peers. You’re open to feedback, and you bring a solutions-oriented mindset to the table. Experience with LLMs, prompt engineering, and building applications powered by GenAI. Proven track record of delivering software that made it into production and is actively used by users. Exposure to working in cloud-native environments (e.g., AWS, GCP, Azure). Experience using observability tools to understand and troubleshoot system behavior. Bonus Points for: Experience building or working with agent frameworks or multi‑agent workflows. Experience as a data analyst or work with data platforms (e.g., Looker, Tableau, PowerBI, Snowflake, DataBricks) Experience building tools for data engineering. How we work: We are a remote-first team that meets regularly over video and does most of our work asynchronously, in writing. We value creativity, diverse perspectives, and clear communication. Tempo is relied upon by prominent global organizations to monitor critical applications and infrastructure, and we expect everyone on the team, including our Staff engineers, to contribute ideas that make it a more reliable, more useful, and more loved product. Compensation & Rewards: In Spain, the Base compensation range for this role is EUR 94,025 - EUR 112,830. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally. *Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process. Why You’ll Thrive at Grafana Labs: 100% Remote, Global Culture - As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose. Scaling Organization – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment. Transparent Communication – Expect open decision-making and regular company-wide updates. Innovation-Driven – Autonomy and support to ship great work and try new things. Open Source Roots – Built on community-driven values that shape how we work. Empowered Teams – High trust, low ego culture that values outcomes over optics. Career Growth Pathways – Defined opportunities to grow and develop your career. Approachable Leadership – Transparent execs who are involved, visible, and human. Passionate People – Join a team of smart, supportive folks who care deeply about what they do. In-Person onboarding - We want you to thrive from day 1 with your fellow new ‘Grafanistas’ to learn all about what we do and how we do it. Balance is Key - We operate a global annual leave policy of 30 days per annum. 3 days of your annual leave entitlement are reserved for Grafana Shutdown Days to allow the team to really disconnect. *We will comply with local legislation where applicable. Equal Opportunity Employer: Grafana Labs is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from everyone regardless of race, colour, nationality, origin, caste, sex, gender reassignment identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, religion or belief, disability, veteran status, genetic information, pregnancy, maternity, marital, family or carer status, or any other characteristic which is protected by local law. We believe that equality and diversity build a strong organisation, and we work hard to ensure that is the foundation of our organisation as we grow. Grafana Labs may utilize AI tools in its recruitment process to assist in matching information provided in CVs to job postings. The recruitment team will continue to review inbound CVs manually to identify alignment with current openings. #LI-Remote For information about how your personal data is used once you’ve applied to a job, check out our privacy policy .

title: Customer Support Operations
description: I quit medicine because I kept watching patients die needlessly, for avoidable reasons. In almost every case, the medical knowledge and clinicians were there. It was the system that failed: the way information moved, decisions got routed, and fragmented teams and data turned solvable problems into tragedy. I started Anima to change that. Our mission is human wellbeing, and we believe personalised medicine will transform it. Our founding insight is that getting there requires a system that learns continuously from care and its outcomes, optimising for human wellbeing. Building that learning engine is the opportunity at the heart of Anima. We're now in 1,000+ clinics across 5 product lines, serving more than 25% of the UK population. We are cash flow positive, growing fast, and have a tight crew of ~45 people who care deeply for each other and the mission. Everyone has real ownership and a voice in decisions. Multiple trillion-dollar companies will be built in healthcare over the next two decades. We intend to be one of them. If you want to work on problems where the stakes are high, you belong at Anima. Your work here will save lives. -- Shun £25k–£75k base, depending on location and experience, plus equity Remote, UK time zone The role When a clinic gets stuck, you’ll help them move forward. You’ll become an expert in Anima, untangle technical problems and give clinicians and practice teams clear, practical answers. This is a hands-on IC role with real ownership of how support develops at Anima. You’ll resolve customer issues while helping build the function: deciding what to measure, improving how the team works and shaping what excellent support looks like as we scale. What you’ll do Own issues through to resolution. Support customers through Intercom, email and short video calls. Investigate thoroughly, keep people informed and follow through. Make technical problems actionable. Reproduce bugs and give engineers clear steps, relevant logs and customer impact. Help distinguish product issues from gaps in understanding or setup. Make answers easier to find. Turn useful solutions into Help Centre articles, internal guidance and short walkthroughs. Build the support function. Identify what’s holding the team back and own improvements—from how we measure quality and prioritise work to the systems, playbooks and automations we use. Test new approaches, see whether they work and help the whole team improve. Bring customer insight into the business. Help Product understand where users struggle, and work with Implementation and Customer Success when an issue needs broader attention. Success means customers get accurate answers quickly, issues reach a clear resolution, and the team gets better at preventing or handling the next one. What you’ll bring Practical problem-solving. Evidence of getting to the bottom of unfamiliar problems, testing possible explanations and finding a workable solution. Clear, empathetic communication. The ability to explain a complicated issue simply, adapt to different levels of technical confidence and build trust with frustrated customers. High agency and drive. Examples of improving a process or building something useful—and seeing it through. Reliability under pressure. Good judgement about urgency, careful follow-through and the ability to manage several conversations without losing track. Curiosity about how products work. An appetite for learning Anima in depth and working closely with engineers to resolve problems. Relevant experience could come from customer support, technical operations, implementation or another role involving complex products and direct customer interaction. Experience with support platforms or process automation is useful; your judgement and results matter more than familiarity What we offer Anima should be where you do your life’s best work. We support that with: Time off: 25 days’ annual leave plus 8 UK public holidays, with flexible additional time off. Health cover: private medical, dental, vision and mental health insurance. Parental leave: 12 weeks’ maternity leave at full pay, rising to 24 weeks after two years; 4 weeks’ paternity leave at full pay. Pension: 4% employer contributions, with salary sacrifice and 100% of the employer National Insurance savings passed on to you. Learning: £1,000 annual budget for your development. Fitness: gym subscription matching up to £50 per month. Equipment: a high-spec MacBook and a home office budget. Time together: two full-team off-sites each year, previous destinations include Mykonos and Mexico. Farringdon office: a beautiful new London HQ, with most of the team together at least twice a week. Everyone is welcome at Anima. We strongly believe in building a diverse and inclusive team. If you’re excited by our mission and believe you could do this work well, we’d love to hear from you, even if your experience doesn’t match every point above. If adjustments would help you participate fully in the interview process, please let us know.

title: English to Bulgarian Medical Devices Linguist
description: About Welo Life Sciences Welo Life Sciences, a Welo Global brand, is a specialized language and technology partner serving pharmaceutical, CRO, and medical device organizations operating in regulated global markets. We deliver regulator-ready translation, linguistic validation, and localization solutions that support clinical trials, pharmacovigilance, regulatory affairs, labeling, and global commercialization. Our approach combines subject matter expertise with ISO-certified quality processes and technology-enabled workflows designed to integrate seamlessly into life sciences operations. With extensive experience supporting global product development and post-market requirements, Welo Life Sciences helps organizations accelerate timelines, protect data integrity, and maintain compliance across languages and regions. All solutions are delivered within a secure, audit-ready framework supported by seven ISO certifications. welolifesciences.com About the Role We are looking for experienced English into Bulgarian linguists specializing in Medical Devices and In Vitro Diagnostics (IVD) documentation translation and review. Key Responsibilities Translate medical device and in vitro diagnostics documentation from English (US) into Bulgarian. Perform Copy Edit (translation review) of translated content, ensuring accuracy, terminology consistency, and compliance with project-specific quality requirements. Review and address QA feedback and client feedback on flagged linguistic issues. Meet agreed deadlines and maintain consistent quality across assigned projects. In Vitro Diagnostics (IVD): Diagnostic product documentation, instructions, labeling and related medical content. Previous experience working with medical device manufacturers, IVD companies, CROs or other Life Sciences organizations. title: Senior Manager, Integrated Marketing Campaigns
description: About Nebius : Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure. Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI. Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D. The Opportunity Nebius is looking for an experienced integrated campaign marketer to turn audience insight into campaigns that grow brand awareness, reach the right customers, and generate qualified demand. You will own the strategy and execution of city-specific campaigns, campaigns around our biggest events, and evergreen campaigns connecting a defined persona with a relevant solution. This is a senior, hands-on individual contributor role. You will research audiences, build campaign plans, write briefs, guide execution, and measure results. You will lead cross-functional teams and agencies without direct line authority, with the opportunity to grow into a team lead as the function evolves. What you will own Own local and evergreen city-specific campaigns . Research priority markets, target personas, buying behaviours, local communities, trusted influencers, and trade publications. Translate those insights into integrated plans that combine the digital and physical channels most relevant to each audience. Build campaigns around major events . Own the integrated campaign plan before, during, and after tier 1 and selected tier 2 events. Partner with Events to extend Nebius awareness and customer reach through digital media, physical activations, influencers, third-party publications, content syndication, and coordinated follow-up. Develop evergreen and solution campaigns . Build sustained programs around a specific persona, business need, and Nebius solution. Create launch activations and ongoing campaigns for priorities such as new hardware, industry use cases, inference, and agentic AI, tailoring messages, offers, and channels to the intended outcome. Turn strategy into execution . Define campaign objectives, customer journeys, channel roles, asset requirements, budgets, timelines, and responsibilities. Write clear briefs, manage dependencies, and work directly with channel owners and agencies to launch coherent campaigns and resolve execution gaps. Lead across teams . Align Product Marketing, Brand / Creative, Content, Digital, Events, Partner Marketing, Sales, and Marketing Operations around one campaign plan. Secure commitments, clarify decisions, and connect campaign engagement to relevant sales or nurture follow-up. Activate partners . Identify where partners add audience access, credibility, or distribution. Develop co-branded content and joint activations with clear shared objectives, responsibilities, follow-up plans, and measures of success. Own agency and vendor performance . Select and brief partners, define scope, deliverables, budgets, and quality standards, and hold them accountable for execution and results. Provide actionable feedback and manage spend and trade-offs throughout the campaign. Define measurement and attribution . Agree baselines, KPIs, tracking, and reporting with Marketing Operations and analytics before launch. Assess awareness, target-audience engagement, qualified demand, pipeline contribution, and efficiency against campaign goals. Use controlled tests or geographic comparisons where feasible and distinguish attributed results from incremental impact. Build repeatable, AI-powered campaign systems. Turn persona research, channel selection, briefs, journey maps, and measurement plans into reusable frameworks that use AI to generate a first version of the customer journey, creative, and cross-channel activations within days, then refine with feedback to launch within weeks. Build in feedback loops that use campaign signals and results to automate improvements to audience targeting, creative, channel mix, and budget allocation—enabling one person to scale across different campaign types. Use AI to accelerate the work . Apply AI to persona and market research, campaign planning, and rapid prototyping of assets and customer journeys. Validate findings and creative quality, document effective workflows, and use the time saved to test and improve campaigns. What success looks like Within 90 days, establish a prioritized campaign roadmap, an agreed measurement framework, and initial audience and market insights, with the first priority campaign launched. Deliver coordinated local, event, and evergreen campaigns with clear audience choices, channel rationale, ownership, and follow-up. Demonstrate improvements in awareness, relevant customer reach, qualified engagement, and pipeline contribution against agreed campaign baselines and goals. Keep teams, agencies, and partners aligned on commitments, delivering campaigns on time and within agreed budgets. Build a repeatable campaign framework that reduces planning and launch time and turns measured results into better campaign decisions. What you bring 8+ years of experience in integrated campaigns, demand generation, or Account-based marketing, including significant hands-on ownership of multi-channel programs at scale. Minimum of 4-5 years leading integrated campaigns for 1 or 2 companies. A proven record of delivering integrated campaigns with measurable business outcomes. You can explain your personal contribution, what worked, what did not, and how those lessons changed your approach. Strong audience and market research skills. You can identify decision-makers, understand their needs and trusted sources, and explain why particular messages, channels, and offers will reach them. Experience combining digital and physical channels into a connected customer journey, with sound judgment about local relevance, event amplification, and sustained demand creation. Creative thinking about media and activation. You see opportunities beyond traditional formats, turning local partnerships, street marketing, and unexpected touchpoints into relevant ways to reach your audience. title: Assurance Lead
description: I quit medicine because I kept watching patients die needlessly, for avoidable reasons. In almost every case, the medical knowledge and clinicians were there. It was the system that failed: the way information moved, decisions got routed, and fragmented teams and data turned solvable problems into tragedy. I started Anima to change that. Our mission is human wellbeing, and we believe personalised medicine will transform it. Our founding insight is that getting there requires a system that learns continuously from care and its outcomes, optimising for human wellbeing. Building that learning engine is the opportunity at the heart of Anima. We're now in 1,000+ clinics across 5 product lines, serving more than 25% of the UK population. We are cash flow positive, growing fast, and have a tight crew of ~45 people who care deeply for each other and the mission. Everyone has real ownership and a voice in decisions. Multiple trillion-dollar companies will be built in healthcare over the next two decades. We intend to be one of them. If you want to work on problems where the stakes are high, you belong at Anima. Your work here will save lives. -- Shun Assurance Lead Healthcare organisations need confidence that the technology they use is clinically safe, protects patient data and can withstand serious scrutiny. At Anima, assurance is not a box-ticking function: it shapes how we build, earn customer trust and bring our technology to more clinicians and patients. We’re looking for an intellectually sharp, pragmatic assurance leader to build and own this function. What you’ll do Shape product decisions. Work closely with Product and Engineering to understand how Anima operates, identify risks early and translate clinical, regulatory and data-protection requirements into practical decisions. Build the assurance function. Own the systems, documentation and processes behind customer and product assurance—including DPIAs, clinical-safety documentation and customer assurance materials. Turn fragmented work into a dependable, scalable function. Lead external assurance. Build trust with ICBs, clinical directors and other healthcare leaders. Explain complex issues clearly, handle challenging questions credibly and support important commercial conversations. Who we’re looking for Demonstrates exceptional critical thinking and systems-level judgement. Can understand complex products and work credibly with Product and Engineering. Has built or substantially improved a function, system or operating process. Can distinguish material risk from process for its own sake. Communicates with authority in difficult customer and stakeholder conversations. Thrives in ownership, ambiguity and a fast-moving technology company. Experience in high-performing medtech or healthtech organisations—particularly those working with the NHS—would be especially valuable. Experience in clinical safety, data protection, DPIAs or healthcare assurance is useful, but we care more about your ability to think, learn and build than whether you have owned every framework. This is a hands-on individual-contributor role with significant ownership. Success means assurance is embedded in how Anima builds, customers trust our answers and teams can move quickly without compromising safety or patient trust. What we offer We are exceptionally selective about who we hire at Anima. As a consequence, we are very generous with our team about the benefits we offer. Anima should be where you do your life’s very best work. Competitive compensation and meaningful equity. 25 days leave plus 8 UK public holidays with flexible additional time off. Private health insurance covering medical, dental, vision and mental health. 12 weeks maternity leave at full pay (rising to 24 weeks after 2 years), 4 weeks paternity at full pay. 4% employer pension contributions with full salary sacrifice and 100% NI savings passed to you. $1,000 annual learning budget. Gym subscription matching up to £50 per month. High-spec MacBook plus home office budget. Two full-team off-sites per year (we've previously gone to Mykonos, Dominican Republic, Mexico, Florida). Hybrid from Farringdon, at least 2 days a week in person. What we offer Anima should be where you do your life’s best work. We support that with: Time off: 25 days’ annual leave plus 8 UK public holidays, with flexible additional time off. Health cover: private medical, dental, vision and mental health insurance. Parental leave: 12 weeks’ maternity leave at full pay, rising to 24 weeks after two years; 4 weeks’ paternity leave at full pay. Pension: 4% employer contributions, with salary sacrifice and 100% of the employer National Insurance savings passed on to you. Learning: £1,000 annual budget for your development. Fitness: gym subscription matching up to £50 per month. Equipment: a high-spec MacBook and a home office budget. Time together: two full-team off-sites each year, previous destinations include Mykonos and Mexico. Farringdon office: a beautiful new London HQ, with most of the team together at least twice a week. Everyone is welcome at Anima. We strongly believe in building a diverse and inclusive team. If you’re excited by our mission and believe you could do this work well, we’d love to hear from you, even if your experience doesn’t match every point above. If adjustments would help you participate fully in the interview process, please let us know.

title: Senior / Lead Program Manager
description: About Nebius : Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure. Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI. Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. You will work at the intersection of strategy, finance, commercial negotiations and execution. Your focus will be to turn complex partnership opportunities into clear business cases, workable commercial terms and agreements that support the needs of Nebius, our partners and our customers. This role suits someone who combines structured problem-solving with strong financial understanding and the ability to move work forward across multiple teams. You should be comfortable assessing commercial trade-offs, bringing clarity to ambiguous problems and taking responsibility for progress. Build the operational framework, track and report progress, develop commercial guidelines Build business cases with Finance. Shape contractual and legal structures. Partner with Legal and relevant business teams to translate the commercial model into practical structures and agreements for partners and customers. Prepare decisions and recommendations. Turn complex information into clear options, explain trade-offs and help stakeholders reach informed decisions. Develop repeatable ways of working. Capture lessons from individual partnerships and improve the frameworks, templates and processes that support the model as it grows. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to break down unfamiliar, complex problems and develop practical recommendations. Financial fluency: you can read and work with financial models, challenge assumptions and explain the commercial implications of the numbers. A specialist financial analyst background is not required. Experience developing business cases, assessing commercial opportunities or supporting complex transactions and partnerships. Confidence working with commercial terms and contracts alongside finance and legal specialists. Strong stakeholder management skills, including the ability to align teams with different priorities and influence without formal authority. The initiative and judgment to drive projects independently, manage ambiguity and recognise when a decision needs wider input. Clear written and verbal communication, particularly when presenting analysis and recommendations to senior stakeholders. Revenue operations background: Supporting sales or partnership teams with clear processes, compensation structure etc. Experience that would be valuable Work on large, complex projects in data centres, digital infrastructure, real estate, power or related sectors. Revenue operations background: supporting sales or partnership teams with clear processes, compensation structure etc. Exposure to partnership models, infrastructure economics or arrangements involving several commercial counterparties. Experience taking a strategic recommendation through negotiation and into implementation. Sector experience is valuable, but we are also interested in strong generalists who can learn a new business model quickly and apply sound commercial judgment.
