title: Senior Engineering Manager, Product Engineering
description: Location: Remote (EMEA) · Germany/Munich preferred - CET/CEST time zone Hi — I'm Grigory, co-founder and CTO at Secfix. At Secfix we're building security compliance systems for teams and agents to become and stay compliant with less effort. We're already the category leader in Europe. AI is changing how software gets built, and we're shaping the tools this new era requires. I've spent most of my career believing that the best engineering leaders aren't the ones who run the most meetings. They're the ones who make everyone around them faster, clearer, and more proud of their work — and they can do that because they've been through the hard technical problems themselves. Since we started, I've done the engineering management myself: 1:1s, hiring, design reviews, performance conversations. The team is 8 engineers and 2 product designers, and I'm spread across too many things. If we were a football team, we'd be a good regional side that just made it to the Bundesliga — talented, hard-working, winning quite a few games. Now we need a coach who's played at Champions League level and can take us there to win every week. That means a strong engineering manager who can still ship. Someone who owns the technical decisions, sets the pace, and has product taste — who notices when a feature takes three weeks that should take one, and when it ships on time but isn't good enough. You won't ship weekly — you'll need focus — but you'll build with the team often enough to know the playbook still works. You'll work directly with me. Two things matter most here: speed and taste. Most teams pick one. We need both to win. — Grigory Why Secfix exists Over 1.78 million SMBs in Europe need to comply with security frameworks — ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, SOC 2 — just to sell to enterprise customers. The process is manual, painful, and takes over a year. We automated it. Our platform integrates with a company's full tech stack — AWS, Azure AD, Jira, GitLab, GCP, and more — automatically extracts compliance evidence, and guides teams to certification in weeks instead of months. Our fastest customer was certified in 4 weeks instead of the industry-standard 12+ months. We've raised €17M in total (€12M Series A), backed by Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital. We're on a profitable trajectory, growing fast, and building the team that will take us to own European market from SMBs to mid market. This space is not threatened by AI; it's amplified by it. Compliance requires deep domain expertise combined with automation. Our new AI product (CISO AI) is just getting started, and there's a huge amount of engineering work ahead: agentic workflows, intelligent evidence collection, context-aware policy generation, and more. What you'll actually do in the first 3 months This isn't a role where you show up and start running standups. There are no standups. Here's how the first quarter goes: Month 1: Ship. Get into the codebase and ship a meaningful feature with AI alongside the team. You don't need to be the fastest engineer in the room, but the team needs to see that you can build at the level you'll ask of them and can ask the right questions. Month 2: Make the team faster. Find where features take three weeks that should take one, and fix it — in tooling, in how we review and test, or in who's working on what. Start regular 1:1s with each engineer, focused on weekly output, quality, and how well they use AI. Month 3: Own hiring. Take over engineering interviews and build a process that runs without my oversight. Design the technical challenges, run the screens, make the calls. The next people we bring in should raise the pace again. I will be there but switch my focus to final interviews. What will the role look like beyond the first 3 months? After the first quarter, the job is management and the technical decisions. You own how the team builds: how engineers test, how they review each other's code and security, how the team is organised, and who we hire next. We're 8 engineers and 2 product designers today and plan to be around 16 within 12 months — most of that hiring is yours to run. You won't ship weekly, but you'll build something with the team now and then, because that's how you know the playbook still gets things out the door. Our CS and Sales leaders work the same way — they still own a small slice of the IC work, so they have skin in the game. Here's what you'll be close to in the next months: Speed. You’ll refine our software development processes to keep the team operating at high velocity. Cycle time from spec to production is your number and accountability. Tooling, review flow, how work is split, who's on what — whatever moves it. Quality. Improve how engineers test and automate, how they review each other's code and security changes, and how the zero-bug policy survives a team of 20. Team and hiring. Team structure, growth conversations, the hiring process, and eventually the next manager. AI in the craft — and in the management. Engineers already work with an established set of encoded skills and rules — there's a whole playbook; you keep pushing that. Same for your own work: hiring, 1:1s, the recurring stuff. What success looks like At 6 months: The hiring process runs without me, and we've added 2 engineers through it. Sales, CS, and product all feel the difference in how fast we ship — and in quality. Our agentic engineering playbook is noticeably better because of you — you’ve added or rewritten the skills, rules, and AI review checks the team uses every day, and you lead by example in how you ship with agents. At 12 months: The team is around 12-16, the zero-bug policy is still holding at that size, and I'm not in the engineering critical path anymore. You've found and/or coached the EM Nr. 2 to support growth. How we work We've written in depth about our engineering culture. Here's the short version — read the full articles linked below if you want the real picture. Focus is sacred. Engineers are in fewer than 2 hours of meetings per week. We write before we meet. We use Loom for async walkthroughs, Notion for specs, Gather for pairing, and Slack only for what's urgent or lightweight. We don't do status theatre. We wrote about our thoughtful communication and our remote culture ; give it a read. To drive it home, here's a recent calendar of an engineer who has been with us for over a year: Small, temporary teams. A designer and two engineers. A backend engineer and a CS person. The group forms around the problem, ships, and dissolves. No standing squads, no permanent team structures — at least not yet. The people closest to the problem usually shape the solution. AI is already part of the craft. We use Claude for product design exploration and spec drafting. Engineers work in Cursor with encoded skills and rules that live in the codebase — component patterns, folder structure, architecture choices, and the path from Figma to Angular code. AI checks code against architecture rules before human review. We have a dedicated design QA skill that compares Figma against coded output. We don't use AI to lower the bar; we use it to reach the bar faster with more iterations behind us. In case you’re interested, we wrote a piece about it here . Zero-bugs. We take this seriously - this helps us to gain customer trust faster. Especially serious customer-facing problems don't sit in a backlog competing with roadmap work. Critical issues get fixed immediately. High-severity within 48 hours. Every bug has an owner. Weekly quality review as part of Monday planning. Quality as identity, in compliance, being correct isn't a nice-to-have; it's the entire value proposition. We care about edge cases, data integrity, and getting the details right. Customers notice the speed and polish before they can name it. That kind of quality builds trust. In our category, trust is the product. We build what customers need , not what they ask for. Customer feedback is signal, not instructions. Best products are built by people with great taste who treat feedback as signals, not KPIs. We stay close to customers — CS check-ins, support tickets, Mixpanel events, onboarding calls — but none of these sources makes the decision for us. This role is for you if: You've managed a real team and made it ship faster. You've hired for it, run the hard conversations, and know what breaks as it grows — and you can point to where cycle time dropped because of you. You know what great engineers look like. You've thought deeply about what makes them productive, what holds them back, and how to move them forward — and you can spot one in a single interview. You have an exceptional IC track record before becoming a manager. You were a senior/principal engineer before you started managing — you didn't skip into management early because coding wasn't working out. You have product taste. You notice when a feature ships on time but isn't good enough, and you say so. You hold people to a high standard. You're comfortable giving direct feedback and having hard conversations about performance. You're hands-on with AI-assisted development. You've used Cursor and Claude Code in real production work, not just toy projects. You have opinions about how AI changes the engineering workflow from ideation to release, and you want to push a team to keep getting faster. You've worked in startups. You know what it feels like when there's low process, and the answer is "figure it out and ship it." You think engineering culture can stay startup-like at scale. You're optimistic that a small, high-performing team can stay that way as it grows, with little process. You communicate proactively in writing. In a remote team, written communication is how decisions get made and context gets shared. But you're not scared of jumping into a pair programming session either. What we're looking for Required 8+ years as a software engineer, including 4+ years managing a team of 8+ and hiring for it yourself You've shipped AI features to production — retrieval, RAG, agentic workflows — and you know the difference between a demo that works and one that holds up on real customer data Product taste: a keen sense for what makes a product feel great, and the habit of saying so when it doesn't You've built and shipped with Claude Code and Cursor in real production work, and you have opinions about where AI helps and where it quietly creates debt You're an engineer at heart. You were senior or principal before you managed, and you can still hold your own in a design review, a debugging session, or building a feature You've built something zero to one at a startup, or scaled a team through the messy middle. You know what it feels like when there's no playbook Able to work in European timezone (CET/CEST). EMEA-based, ideally Germany or UK Nice to have You've grown a team to 15+ at a VC-funded startup Managed tech leads or a second manager Previous experience at a fully remote company Interview process We want to see how you think, build, and lead — not test you on algorithms. Here's the process: 30 min — Intro call with our talent team 45 min — Interview with Grigory 60 min — Technical interview 1.5 hr — AI-assisted build session: system design for a real feature, then building part of it with AI 2 hr — Leadership session with the founders Then you’ll get the offer! If we don't make an offer, we'll tell you why. What Secfix gives you Remote: 100% remote with a real virtual office in Gather Salary: Competitive, benchmarked to European market rates (we'll share specifics once we talk) Equity: Generous package — we're all owners here Development budget: €1,000/year — yours to spend on whatever makes you better Workspace: Remote workspace support + co-working access Holidays: 26 days + local public holidays Health insurance: Comprehensive coverage Annual retreat: Last time we went to Alicante 🇪🇸 — before that, the Austrian Alps, Portugal, Italy, and the Spanish Islands

title: Senior/Staff Platform Engineer - Rust (d/f/m)
description: 🤓 About Luminovo At Luminovo , we’re building the infrastructure that turns the electronics supply chain into something software can read and act on. Our customers use it to quote PCBAs faster, find cost savings and act on risks in their supply chain. We serve 300+ customers, from Europe’s largest EMS to category-leading OEMs, with around 100 Luminerds across Munich, Berlin, New York and Austin. We’re backed by Chalfen Ventures, Cherry Ventures and General Catalyst. With data centers and robotics driving demand for electronics, someone needs to manage that supply chain, and they’ll need good software to do it. ( Here’s why we care so much about electronics .) 🚀 Your role Team Core is our platform team. Its job is to make all our other engineering teams more productive and to improve our codebase and infrastructure as a whole. You’ll: Keep our DevOps setup and CI/CD pipelines fast and reliable Build tools every team needs (e.g. interface for building permissions) Act as an in-house Rust expert: our backend is a Rust monolith, and Team Core helps the other teams use good Rust patterns and architecture Be responsible for the Developer Experience (DX). Help our engineers use agents more productively Other details Location: remote-first, within two hours of CET. We prefer Munich > Berlin > Germany > Europe. Tech stack: Rust, TypeScript + React, Postgres, Clickhouse, Redis, Kafka, Kubernetes, Helm, Flux 🇺🇸 Some of the work in this role falls under US export control regulations (ITAR), so you must be a US citizen . You’ll need to be based in Europe, and if you’re currently in the US, we’ll support your relocation to Germany. 🖲️ Our tech stack We always try to use the best tools available for the job. Don't worry, we don't need you to be familiar with all of these: Main monolith is written in Rust (using actix-web as our web framework), deployed on Kubernetes React and Typescript for frontend PostgreSQL for persisting our data Redis for caching and queues Flux for GitOps Honeycomb, Prometheus and Grafana for monitoring and observability garden-io for developing on Kubernetes Azure and Cloudflare for cloud computing 🤓 Whom you’ll be working with Timon , one of our Founders Alex and Tomas , two of our Staff Engineers Inga , Senior Software Engineer ⚡️ Skills, knowledge, and expertise Just so you know – we purposefully did not create a standard list of minimum qualifications for this role. title: Software Engineer AI Tooling
description: About Supabase Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth. About the Role Weâre looking for a Software Engineer to join our AI Tooling team and help shape how developers and agents build with Supabase. You'll build and own our AI tooling, including agents, the MCP server, agent skills and the dashboard assistant, and as the space moves you'll build the tooling for new technologies too. You'll build it all eval-first: every tool ships with evals and metrics, so we know, with evidence, that it makes agents better rather than worse. You'll work closely with the Docs, CLI, Frontend and SDK teams, and with the AI Tooling Infrastructure engineers who run these services in production. Other teams contribute to AI Tooling to improve Supabase's agentic capabilities, and you'll help them do that while keeping the quality bar high. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions. What Youâll Be Responsible For Build and improve the AI tooling we run today, including the MCP server, agent skills, agents and the Assistant. Make new Supabase products usable by agents from day one: tools, skills and evals for new product surfaces. Also build tooling for new AI technologies as they emerge: prototype quickly, evaluate honestly, and decide with the team what is worth taking to production. Drive an eval-first approach: build and improve evals, instrumentation and feedback loops, measure tools against a no-tool baseline, and help define the quality KPIs and gates that stop regressions shipping. Understand how customers and agents actually use what we ship, and turn that into improvements to our tooling, interfaces and documentation. Design how documentation and product knowledge are exposed to agents, and measure whether it works. Build patterns and tools that help customers add AI to their own apps, such as MCP on Edge Functions, vector embeddings and agents running on Edge Functions. Enable teams to improve Supabase's agentic capabilities through contributions to AI Tooling: clear contribution paths, templates, documentation and review practice. Centralise shared AI logic so teams reuse it rather than duplicate it. Ship tools that are battle-tested, with strong tests, benchmarking and stress testing where it counts. Work with the AI Tooling Infrastructure engineers on reliability, auth and hosting. Work across Docs, CLI, Frontend, SDK and other teams to deliver one coherent developer experience, and stay close to the fast-moving AI ecosystem. You Might Be a Good Fit If You Must have: Have 5+ years of experience in professional software engineering experience. Write strong TypeScript and know the JavaScript ecosystem well: npm, ES modules, bundlers, compatibility. Are deeply familiar with the AI ecosystem: current tools, agent patterns and practical trade-offs. You can tell a durable pattern from hype. Have built developer tools, product interfaces or platform primitives used by other engineers. Have designed or used evaluation frameworks to measure AI quality, reliability and task success, and understand baselines, variance and cost. Have strong judgement about where AI improves workflows and how to avoid fragile or gimmicky experiences. Write tests and validate reliability in real-world conditions. Know Postgres and relational database practice. Communicate clearly in writing, work across product, engineering and docs, and thrive in async, globally distributed teams. Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and moving quickly. Nice to have: Experience with vector databases and embeddings, ideally pgvector. Examples of customer-facing AI features or agents you've shipped. Examples of documentation or structured knowledge designed for developers or agents. Experience with Braintrust or a similar eval and tracing platform, or setting up CI quality gates. Open-source contributions or developer tooling you've maintained. Experience across several product surfaces or teams. What We Offer Fully Remote We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world. ESOP Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what weâre building together. Tech Allowance Use this budget to set up your ideal work environmentâlaptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work. Health Benefits Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your familyâs health are important to us. Annual Off-Sites Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. Itâs a highlight of our year. Flexible Work We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when. Professional Development Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learningâcourses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth. About the Team Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love. ~400 team members 60+ countries 20+ languages spoken Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F) 540,000+ community members We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If itâs in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to supportânot replaceâexisting tools and communities. title: UX Research Intern
description: About baesh baesh is a social platform connecting people in real life through events, communities, and shared interests. We’re a small team using AI to move quickly from ideas to working experiences. Research is central to how we decide what to build and whether it’s good enough to ship. Your work will help us stay close to people as the technology moves faster. You’ll work closely with our Head of Product and UX , an experienced researcher with a PhD in emotional and behavioural research. You’ll get practical guidance across the research process—from deciding what to investigate to helping the team act on what we learn. This is an unpaid mandatory internship for students whose university programme requires a placement. Location: Mostly remote, with opportunities to join research and events in Berlin. Start date: Flexible, depending on your university requirements. Duration: As required by your university, usually 3–6 months. What you’ll help with Usability testing and idea validation Help plan and run usability tests on our app and prototypes, including interfaces built with AI. Explore how easily people can discover events, join communities, and create their profiles. Test whether experiences make sense to real people, beyond looking polished or functioning technically. Validate early ideas and assumptions before the team invests further. Identify confusing moments and recommend improvements that make a meaningful difference. Exploratory research and interviews Help interview existing users and people who haven’t tried baesh yet. Explore how people make friends, find things to do, and connect with communities. Understand their needs, motivations, habits, and barriers. Help write discussion guides and ask open questions that uncover useful insights. Bring people’s experiences into product decisions, keeping the human connection at the heart of how we build. AI-supported research Use AI to help draft interview guides, usability-testing scripts, and survey questions. Explore how AI can support research synthesis by organising notes, summarising sessions, and suggesting patterns. Check AI-generated summaries and interpretations against what participants actually said and did. Learn where AI saves time, where it misses nuance, and where your judgement matters most. Help us develop practical ways to combine faster research workflows with thoughtful, reliable findings. Recruitment and ongoing feedback Help recruit participants and coordinate research sessions. Support Friends of BAESH , our community of early adopters who contribute through interviews, user testing, feedback, and feature suggestions. Help create short in-app surveys about specific parts of the experience. Making sense of what we learn Analyse feedback and identify patterns across sessions. Turn findings into clear insights and practical recommendations. Share research with the product and development team to shape what happens next. Help organise our research so we can build on previous learning. You won’t be expected to do all of this independently from day one. We’ll guide you, give you feedback, and gradually help you take ownership of research activities. What you’ll bring You’re enrolled in a degree programme that requires a mandatory internship. An interest in UX research, psychology, human–computer interaction, design, sociology, or a related field. Curiosity about people and a willingness to question assumptions. Good listening skills and an empathetic, respectful approach. Strong communication skills in English. An organised approach and willingness to take initiative. An interest in using AI thoughtfully, including questioning its output. Preferred, but not required: German-speaking , so you can support research with German-speaking participants. Some familiarity with interviews, usability testing, surveys, or qualitative analysis—university projects count. Experience experimenting with AI tools for research, writing, analysis, or prototyping. An interest in social products, communities, and how digital experiences support real-life connections. You don’t need previous professional UX research experience. We’re looking for curiosity, care, and a willingness to learn. What you’ll gain Research mentorship: Learn directly from an experienced UX and behavioural researcher. Practical experience: Contribute to exploratory interviews, usability testing, surveys, and idea validation. Experience with AI-enabled product development: Learn how to assess and improve products when building is fast and informed judgement matters more than ever. Visible impact: See your findings shape the experiences we build and release. Portfolio experience: Develop research case studies, with guidance on what can be shared. Flexible working: Agree a schedule that fits your university’s placement requirements. A small, collaborative team: Work closely with the people designing and building the product. Interested? If you have relevant university work or a portfolio, we’d love to see it—but it’s optional. Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: Backend Engineer, Trusted Agentic Development
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As an Intermediate Backend Engineer, Trusted Agentic Development, based in Poland, you'll build backend systems that help GitLab engineers trust the software they create with artificial intelligence agents. Agents can generate code and tests in seconds, but passing tests don't always mean the software works as intended. You'll contribute to validation approaches and feedback mechanisms that help agents catch that gap and self-correct while they work.</p> <p>This isn't a quality assurance or test automation role. We’re looking for someone who has built with agents, run into the gap between passing tests and working software, and wants to help close it.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Own backend features from design through production rollout, making the design calls within the architecture the team agrees on.</li> <li>Build agentic code-review and validation workflows that check whether generated code does what was intended, not just whether its tests pass.</li> <li>Prototype focused validation and feedback mechanisms with your teammates, and use what you learn to improve the platform.</li> <li>Develop language-aware validation approaches, starting with Rust, Ruby, and Go, adapting techniques to each language while applying a shared definition of trusted software to assess whether agent-generated code delivers the intended behavior.</li> <li>Implement feedback that helps agents identify problems and self-correct during development.</li> <li>Collaborate with engineering teams to test these approaches in real workflows, measure adoption, engineer trust, and validation quality, and use those measurements to evaluate improvements.</li> <li>Participate in code and design reviews, explain implementation trade-offs, and seek feedback on your work.</li> <li>Take part in on-call or operational support where your team's ownership model requires it.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Hands-on experience building software with artificial intelligence agents and understanding why their output can pass tests yet fail to behave as intended, from encountering that gap yourself or building something to prevent it.</li> <li>Backend development experience in at least one of Rust, Ruby, Go, or Python, with openness to working across languages.</li> <li>Experience taking backend features from design into production, discussing implementation trade-offs, and knowing when to ask for guidance.</li> <li>Comfort working inside a large existing codebase, not only on greenfield projects.</li> <li>A practical approach to prototyping, learning from results, and turning useful ideas into working software.</li> <li>Clear written communication and the ability to collaborate in an all-remote, asynchronous environment.</li> <li>The ability to share decisions transparently and improve your work through iteration and feedback.</li> <li>Familiarity with containerized services; Kubernetes experience is a plus.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>The Trusted Agentic Development team sits within GitLab's Developer Experience group and builds the platforms our engineers rely on every day. We work across engineering teams and programming languages to understand how people use agents, test new approaches in real workflows, and create a shared model of trusted agentic development that teams choose to adopt.</p> <p> </p> <p><strong><em>Poland base salary range:</em></strong><em> zł 248,000 - zł 372,000</em></p> <p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the EU, applicable in the specified country or countries only. Sales roles are also eligible for incentive pay targeted at up to 100% of the offered base salary. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location and having regard to any applicable collective agreements. The base salary range does not include bonuses, equity, or benefits.</em></p> <h2><br><br></h2><div class="content-conclusion"><h4><strong>How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees</strong></h4> <ul> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/">Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/#flexible-paid-time-off-pto">Flexible Paid Time Off </a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/company/culture/inclusion/tmrg-tmag/">Team Member Resource Groups</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/stock-options/">Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/learning-and-development/growth-and-development/">Growth and Development Fund</a></li> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave">Parental Leave</a> </li> </ul> <p>Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. Additionally, studies have shown that people from <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/company/culture/inclusion/#examples-of-select-underrepresented-groups">underrepresented groups</a> are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every single qualification. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.</p> <hr> <p><strong>Country Hiring Guidelines: </strong>GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. All of our roles are remote, however some roles may carry specific location-based eligibility requirements. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.  </p> <p><strong>Privacy Policy: </strong>Please review our <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/hiring/candidate-faq/recruitment-privacy-policy/" target="_blank">Recruitment Privacy Policy.</a> Your privacy is important to us.</p> <p>GitLab is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. GitLab’s policies and practices relating to recruitment, employment, career development and advancement, promotion, and retirement are based solely on merit, regardless of race, color, religion, ancestry, sex (including pregnancy, lactation, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression), national origin, age, citizenship, marital status, mental or physical disability, genetic information (including family medical history), discharge status from the military, protected veteran status (which includes disabled veterans, recently separated veterans, active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans, and Armed Forces service medal veterans), or any other basis protected by law. GitLab will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics. See also <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/people-policies/inc-usa/#equal-employment-opportunity-policy" target="_blank">GitLab’s EEO Policy</a> and <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/labor-and-employment-notices/#eeoc-us-equal-employment-opportunity-commission-notices" target="_blank">EEO is the Law</a>. title: Senior Professional Services Engineer - Charlotte, NC
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As a Senior Professional Services Engineer at GitLab, you'll work directly with customers to deliver installation, migration, training, and advisory services that help them adopt GitLab successfully. You'll lead engagements from single-node Omnibus installs to large reference architectures built with infrastructure as code (IaC) and configuration as code. You'll also guide migrations from other systems to GitLab SaaS or self-managed deployments, and help customers make practical decisions that improve reliability, security, and day-to-day workflows.</p> <p>In this role, you'll work closely with customers and GitLab's product and engineering teams to drive customer success and share feedback that improves GitLab and how we deliver services. You'll manage multiple projects at once, mentor other Professional Services Engineers, and help streamline how we deliver consistent outcomes in a remote, largely asynchronous environment.</p> <p>Some examples of our projects:</p> <ul> <li>Designing and delivering GitLab installations and reference architectures using tools like Terraform and Ansible across major cloud providers</li> <li>Leading migrations to GitLab SaaS or self-managed GitLab, and turning customer feedback into actionable improvements for GitLab's product and engineering teams</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Deliver GitLab Professional Services engagements, including installation, migration, training, and advisory services across GitLab capabilities.</li> <li>Plan and execute deployments ranging from single-node Omnibus installations to large reference architectures using Infrastructure as Code and Configuration as Code practices.</li> <li>Lead migrations from multiple source systems to GitLab SaaS or self-managed GitLab, helping customers adopt secure, reliable workflows.</li> <li>Partner with Engagement Managers and Project Managers to improve delivery consistency, remove friction, and continuously refine delivery processes.</li> <li>Serve as a trusted technical advisor for customers, translating goals and constraints into practical implementation plans and clear next steps.</li> <li>Interface with GitLab's product and engineering teams to unblock customer outcomes and share feedback that helps improve GitLab features and services.</li> <li>Mentor Associate and Intermediate Professional Services Engineers, providing technical guidance, helping remove blockers, and supporting increased autonomy.</li> <li>Manage and deliver multiple customer engagements at once, either as the primary engineer or as a lead providing oversight and direction to other engineers.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Professional exposure with one or more infrastructure as code or configuration as code technologies such as Terraform, Ansible, Packer, Puppet, or Chef.</li> <li>Professional exposure with two or more cloud providers such as Amazon Web Services (AWS), Google Cloud Platform (GCP), or Microsoft Azure.</li> <li><strong>This role has a location requirement - Charlotte, NC or nearby - on site at the Customer location in Charlotte, 5 days a week.</strong></li> <li>Experience using, deploying, or configuring GitLab, including a solid understanding of Git and source control workflows.</li> <li>Experience delivering customer-facing services such as installation, migration, training, and advisory engagements across GitLab's feature set.</li> <li>Proven ability to independently manage one or more projects and to lead and provide direction to other Professional Services Engineers on complex engagements.</li> <li>Strong communication skills in English, written and verbal, with the ability to provide clear status updates and build consensus with peers and customers in a remote, largely asynchronous environment.</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to take a solution-oriented approach by identifying root causes, proposing options and tradeoffs, and driving issues to resolution while balancing multiple customer engagements in a fast-paced environment.</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a fully remote organization by communicating clearly in writing, documenting decisions, collaborating asynchronously across time zones, and working in ways consistent with GitLab's values.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>Senior Professional Services Engineers are part of GitLab's Professional Services team. We partner closely with Engagement Managers and Project Managers to deliver consistent outcomes, and we work with GitLab's product and engineering teams to share customer feedback and improve GitLab. Professional Services operates in a fully remote and largely asynchronous environment, collaborating across regions and time zones. The team's challenge is to support customers with a wide range of architectures and deployment models while maintaining high-quality delivery and setting customers up for long-term success.</p> <h4><br><br></h4><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. title: Procurement Lead
description: We’re looking for a Procurement Lead to own the commercial and vendor-management function for Supabase. You’ll run our cloud and SaaS vendor relationships end-to-end (AWS, GCP, Cloudflare, CloudQuery, ClickHouse, and more), leading negotiations and renewals, enforcing procurement governance, and applying our VIA operating model (Visibility, Insights, Actions) to keep vendor spend disciplined and well-governed. You’ll work closely with Finance, Engineering, Legal, and our vendor partners. This is a lead role for the Procurement function. The operating model, the source of truth for vendor spend, and the standards are yours to define, against a clear position: this is a FinOps role first, not a pure procurement desk. You'll own the technical and analytical side of vendor management, reporting, efficiency, and the commercial interface across the company, while keeping procurement governance tight. It's ideal for someone fluent across finance and engineering, who thrives in async, fast-moving environments, and wants to build a function from the ground up rather than inherit one. WHAT YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR In this role, you’ll: - Own vendor relationships: run our primary cloud and SaaS vendor relationships end-to-end (AWS, GCP, Cloudflare, CloudQuery, ClickHouse, and more), leading renewals and negotiations alongside Finance and Legal. - Run procurement governance: enforce our competitive-bid process for incoming requests and manage larger procurement through our managed-procurement partner, keeping oversight and accountability with FinOps. - People management: Build a healthy, high-trust team culture in a remote-first, globally distributed environment. Run 1:1s, performance management, career development, and onboarding for your direct report(s).Handle people admin (leave, time off, etc.) for your team. - Manage team’s delivery and accountability: Own the team's roadmap and project management (Linear), driving accountability and clear milestones. Manage workflow intake and Slack triage. Own the team's weekly updates and keep stakeholders aligned without creating overhead. - Drive commercial VIA: own spend visibility and unit economics, surface licensing and usage inefficiency before it becomes a surprise, and drive renewals, right-sizing, and tooling consolidation to realized savings. - Build reporting and governance: vendor and SaaS cost reporting is the unowned gap today and your highest-leverage area in the first year. Build the dashboards and reporting hands-on, partner with our data teams to scale them, and own the governance layer (spend policies, thresholds, accountability). - Coordinate the cloud efficiency program: keep optimization initiatives visible and tracked from commitment to realized savings, partnering with Engineering without taking over their delivery. YOU MIGHT BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU - Have 8+ years in vendor/commercial management, procurement, FinOps, or technical/financial analysis, at a senior, function-owning level. - Have owned vendor relationships, contract negotiations, and renewals, and treat them as a lever on unit economics. - Have run procurement governance such as competitive-bid processes, benchmark analysis, approval thresholds, or managed-procurement partners. - Have high judgment and can hold a position and drive alignment without positional authority. - Build cost dashboards and reporting hands-on (SQL, BI tools), and are comfortable with vendor and cloud spend data (AWS, GCP, SaaS billing) and licensing/usage analysis. - Communicate clearly across both technical and non-technical audiences. - Have experience in async or globally distributed teams. - Are energized by building a function from the ground up and navigating ambiguity. WHAT WE OFFER - Fully Remote We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world. - ESOP Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together. - Tech Allowance Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work. - Health Benefits Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us. - Annual Off-Sites Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year. - Flexible Work We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when. - Professional Development Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth. ABOUT THE TEAM Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love. - ~400 team members - 60+ countries - 20+ languages spoken - Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F) - 540,000+ community members We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h4><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h4> <p>As Manager, SOX PMO - Business Process, you'll lead Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) compliance for assigned business processes as part of GitLab's second line. This is advisory work, not repeatable testing: you'll deeply understand how processes work, evaluate risks as the business changes, and help control owners design and remediate controls that hold up to audit. Judgment matters more than procedure. You'll form well-supported conclusions, align with control owners and Internal Audit, and defend positions to external auditors. GitLab already uses AI extensively, and the next phase brings AI agents into our SOX processes. You'll help teams adopt them with confidence, finding creative ways to enable new ways of working while maintaining compliance. You'll also partner with the information technology (IT) SOX PMO on readiness for new systems and applications. This role reports to the Senior Director, SOX PMO, within the Chief Accounting Officer's organization.</p> <p><strong>What You’ll Do</strong>  </p> <ul> <li>Lead SOX compliance for assigned business processes as the second-line subject matter expert, advising control owners who own and operate the controls. Deeply understand each process, its systems and data flows, and resolve open questions and assumptions early.</li> <li>Monitor risks from new and changing processes, products, and systems. Help control owners design, strengthen, or right-size controls, and contribute to the annual SOX risk assessment and scoping.</li> <li>Evaluate control deficiencies individually and in aggregate, identify root causes, and prepare well-supported severity assessments. Work with management to develop, implement, and monitor remediation plans.</li> <li>Prepare auditor-ready technical memos on sampling methodology, scoping, and control rationalization, using independent analysis and sound conclusions. Prepare reports and presentations on SOX compliance status for leadership.</li> <li>Lead business walkthroughs and stakeholder meetings, and coordinate with Internal Audit and external auditors throughout the audit. Anticipate questions, support positions with data and judgment, and escalate risks and auditor comments promptly with a recommended path forward.</li> <li>Advise on controls for AI-enabled processes and processes that use AI agents. Find opportunities to automate SOX work using AI tools, and validate their output.</li> <li>Partner with the IT SOX PMO to assess new systems and controls, including application controls and key reports.</li> <li>Develop and maintain accurate process narratives, flowcharts, and risk and control matrices as processes change. Collaborate with Finance, Operations, Legal, Human Resources, Sales, Engineering, and IT leaders to help them design and maintain effective business controls.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You’ll Bring </strong></p> <ul> <li>Hands-on SOX and internal controls experience in control design, remediation, and deficiency evaluation, beyond testing alone. Experience in the software or technology industry is required; SOX PMO, Big Four risk advisory, or assurance experience is a strong plus.</li> <li>A bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field; an active Certified Public Accountant (CPA) credential (strongly preferred) or Certified Internal Auditor (CIA) credential.</li> <li>A strong understanding of SOX requirements and internal control frameworks, such as the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO) framework.</li> <li>Professional judgment and skepticism: verifying facts against source documents, testing the reasonableness of data and conclusions, and recognizing missing information.</li> <li>A track record of independently solving ambiguous, novel problems, from defining an approach through overcoming obstacles and driving resolution. Curiosity to understand how processes actually work and keep learning as the business changes.</li> <li>Clear written and verbal communication, including concise, accurate, auditor-ready memos and actionable recommendations. Confidence partnering with senior stakeholders and external auditors, including working through pushback.</li> <li>A practical, innovative approach to helping the business adopt new technologies, products, and ways of working while maintaining compliance. Experience using AI tools to improve efficiency and validating their output.</li> <li>Experience with usage-based billing or AuditBoard is a plus.</li> </ul> <p><strong>About the team</strong></p> <p>The SOX PMO is part of the Chief Accounting Officer's organization. In this role, you'll advise business control owners and partner with the IT SOX PMO, Internal Audit, and external auditors to keep GitLab compliant as processes, systems, and AI use evolve. GitLab is an all-remote company, with flexibility to work from home or wherever you're most productive. You'll need to be available to collaborate with teammates during core US Pacific (PT) and Eastern (ET) business hours.</p> <h4><strong>How GitLab will support you</strong></h4> <ul> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/" target="_blank">Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/paid-time-off/" target="_blank">Flexible Paid Time Off</a> </li> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/company/culture/inclusion/erg-guide/#:~:text=Definition%20of%20the%20TMRG%20%2D%20Team%20Member%20Resource%20Groups,-TMRGs%20are%20voluntary&text=The%20purpose%20for%20this%20type,developing%20the%20sense%20of%20belonging." target="_blank">Team Member Resource Groups</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/stock-options/" target="_blank">Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/learning-and-development/growth-and-development/" target="_blank">Growth and Development Fund</a></li> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave" target="_blank">Parental leave</a> </li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/finance/expenses/#equipment" target="_blank">Home office</a> support</li> </ul> <p>Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. description: Location: San Francisco or Singapore (on-site), or remote (Singapore or US Pacific time zones) Start Date: ASAP Languages: English Team: Engineering About the Role Our client is a fast-growing AI company building reliable, fair and open infrastructure for AI training data. Their marketplace helps the people who create data get value for it, and gives AI labs trustworthy data to train on. It is already used by startups, Fortune 500 companies and frontier labs, and the company is backed by leading venture investors, including Y Combinator. They are scaling quickly to meet strong demand. We are looking for a Research Engineer, Privacy and Anonymization to build the systems that make sensitive, real-world data safe and still useful for AI training. You will develop methods to detect and remove personally identifiable information, secrets and other sensitive content from raw data before it enters processing and synthetic data pipelines â protecting privacy without destroying the structure and signal that make the data valuable for training agents. This is a privacy and data-protection engineering seat, not a synthetic-task design role. You will own the pipeline that stands in front of downstream processing, training, evaluation and synthetic generation. This is a full-time role, starting ASAP. Offices are in San Francisco and Singapore; remote candidates are welcome if their working hours can overlap about 70â80% with either San Francisco (US Pacific) or Singapore business hours. The exact daily schedule will be agreed during hiring. What You'll Do Build systems to detect PII, quasi-identifiers, credentials and other sensitive information, and design transformations based on the data type and the downstream use case. Develop and benchmark detection approaches that combine rules, statistical models, classifiers and LLM-based methods. Build production pipelines that anonymize raw data before it enters downstream processing, training, evaluation or synthetic data generation. Create evaluation frameworks that measure privacy risk and retained data utility, including recall-weighted metrics, leakage tests and adversarial re-identification attempts. Design systems that stay robust to new data sources, schema drift, unusual formats and sensitive information embedded in unexpected fields. Work with engineering, research, operations and customers to translate privacy requirements into practical technical policies and safeguards. What We're Looking For Strong proficiency in Python, and experience building reliable production data or machine-learning systems. Experience with information extraction, named-entity recognition, classification, or related methods for detecting rare or sensitive content. Strong experimental instincts, and the ability to compare approaches across recall, precision, latency, cost and downstream data utility. An understanding of the difference between redaction, masking, pseudonymization, anonymization and synthetic data â and when each is appropriate. High attention to detail, and the ability to reason about subtle leakage paths, edge cases and adversarial failure modes. Experience building data-processing pipelines end to end, including where there was no fully prescribed roadmap. Clear written and spoken English, and comfort collaborating across teams and time zones. Strong candidates may also have hands-on experience with privacy-enhancing technologies (such as differential privacy, k-anonymity, secure aggregation or format-preserving encryption); have worked with sensitive data in healthcare, finance or security; have built low-latency or high-throughput ML inference or data-processing systems; or have taken work from early research through to production. Technical aptitude and learning potential matter more than years of experience. Motivated candidates are encouraged to apply even if they don't meet every point above. Why This Role Matters for You Make real-world data safe to train on: You will build the systems that let sensitive data be used for AI training without exposing people or secrets. Privacy without wrecking utility: The job is not only to redact, but to keep the structure and signal that downstream training and synthetic pipelines need. From detection to production: You will own the full path: detection methods, transformations, evaluation, and the pipeline that sits in front of training and generation. Hard, high-stakes edge cases: Work on leakage paths, schema drift and adversarial failure modes, not only clean benchmark datasets. San Francisco, Singapore, or remote: Work on-site in San Francisco or Singapore, or remotely, with hours that overlap about 70â80% with either US Pacific or Singapore business hours. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2>An overview of this role</h2> <p>As a Staff Backend Engineer in GitLab's Performance Enablement group, you'll define and build the self-serve platform that lets GitLab engineering teams own their performance. You'll give internal teams the tooling and guidance to run performance tests, analyze results, track trends, and meet their own performance requirements throughout the development lifecycle. We're a platform, not a consulting service: we build capabilities that teams use independently to deliver a reliable, performant GitLab to customers. In this hands-on technical leadership role, you'll work with the Engineering Manager to shape a multi-quarter vision and roadmap, bringing your performance engineering expertise to influence teams across research and development (R&D).</p> <p>Some examples of our projects in <a class="textLink" href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/infrastructure-platforms/developer-experience/performance-enablement/">Performance Enablement</a>:</p> <ul> <li value="1">Building reusable component-level testing, load testing, performance analysis, trend visibility, and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted engineering skills</li> <li value="2">Enabling teams to test performance throughout the development lifecycle, from local development and continuous integration (CI) workflows through pre-release validation, including modular feature teams' own workflows</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Define the team's technical vision and multi-quarter roadmap with the Engineering Manager, identify opportunities for impact across R&D, and advocate for technical priorities with stakeholders.</li> <li value="2">Design and build reusable platform capabilities for performance testing, analysis, reporting, and trend visibility, solving complex technical problems and shipping large capabilities with minimal guidance.</li> <li value="3">Turn lessons from early team engagements into reusable capabilities, documentation, and onboarding, measured by each new team needing less hands-on support than the last until teams can adopt the platform and manage their performance independently.</li> <li value="4">Coordinate with peer teams across Developer Experience, Infrastructure Platforms, and product groups to align priorities and timing.</li> <li value="5">Lead AI-first development practices in how we build and what we ship, including AI skills and agent-assisted performance workflows.</li> <li value="6">Mentor engineers in performance engineering, platform design, and technical decision-making.</li> <li value="7">Serve as a performance expert for other teams and provide technical guidance on initiatives spanning multiple groups.</li> <li value="8">Take part in on-call or operational support where your team's ownership model requires it.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Staff-level backend or platform engineering experience, including setting technical direction across a team and the teams around it.</li> <li value="2">A track record of building and operating performance testing and analysis systems, with an understanding of where bottlenecks appear and how to find them.</li> <li value="3">Experience leading or anchoring a performance enablement or platform function and achieving measurable adoption of internal tooling by influencing engineers and leaders who don't report to you.</li> <li value="4">Experience defining and delivering a multi-quarter technical strategy or roadmap with engineering leadership.</li> <li value="5">An AI-first development mindset demonstrated across the software lifecycle, including shaping how a team uses AI.</li> <li value="6">Hands-on experience with load and performance testing tools such as k6 or equivalent, Kubernetes, and Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud Platform, or similar cloud infrastructure.</li> <li value="7">Clear written, asynchronous communication, including explaining performance trade-offs to engineers and leadership.</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p><a class="textLink" href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/infrastructure-platforms/developer-experience/performance-enablement/">Performance title: Programmatic Advertising Specialist - BENELUX
description: Programmatic Advertising Specialist (Dutch Speaking) Publisher Success | Amsterdam, Netherlands (Onsite) | Full Time | Permanent About Refinery89 Refinery89 is a Dutch AdTech company headquartered in Madrid, working with premium publishers worldwide to optimize programmatic advertising performance. Through advanced, data-driven technology, we help publishers maximize advertising revenue, improve monetization efficiency, and gain greater transparency across their advertising operations. Our international team brings together specialists in programmatic advertising, publisher monetization, technology, and account management to deliver measurable results for our partners. About the Role Are you currently working in Programmatic Advertising, Ad Operations, Campaign Management, or Publisher Monetization and looking to take the next step in your career? We're looking for a Dutch-speaking Programmatic Advertising Specialist to join our Publisher Success team in Amsterdam. This opportunity is ideal for someone with a solid understanding of digital advertising who wants to move beyond campaign execution and take on a more strategic, publisher-facing role. You don't need previous Account Management experience. We're particularly interested in candidates who understand the programmatic advertising ecosystem, enjoy analyzing performance, solving technical challenges, and communicating with clients. You'll work directly with Dutch publishers, helping them optimize their advertising performance, maximize revenue, and develop long-term partnerships with Refinery89. You'll collaborate closely with our Technical Account Managers, AdTech specialists, Product, and Sales teams to deliver the best possible experience for our publishing partners. Key Responsibilities Publisher Relationship Management Build and maintain strong relationships with publishers in the Netherlands. Serve as a primary point of contact for publisher inquiries, performance discussions, and ongoing support. Develop a deep understanding of each publisher's business needs and monetization objectives. Build trust through proactive communication, responsiveness, and problem-solving. Programmatic Performance & Revenue Optimization Monitor and analyze advertising performance, including revenue, eCPM, fill rates, and other relevant programmatic metrics. Identify opportunities to improve publisher monetization and overall advertising performance. Translate advertising data into clear insights and actionable recommendations. Collaborate with technical specialists to implement and evaluate optimization initiatives. Technical Coordination & Troubleshooting Help publishers identify and resolve advertising-related issues. Work closely with internal AdTech and Technical Account Management teams to investigate technical challenges. Coordinate solutions and ensure publishers receive timely updates. Develop a strong understanding of Refinery89's advertising technology and monetization solutions. Strategic Growth & Publisher Success Identify opportunities to grow existing publisher accounts. Support publisher performance reviews and strategic discussions. Share insights about market trends, advertising technologies, and monetization opportunities. Contribute to long-term publisher satisfaction, retention, and growth. Cross-Functional Collaboration Work closely with Publisher Sales, Technical Account Managers, AdTech, Product, and Finance teams. Communicate publisher feedback and market insights internally. Help improve processes, workflows, and the overall publisher experience. What We're Looking For Must-Have Qualifications Native-level Dutch proficiency , with professional working proficiency in English. 1 to 3 years of experience in programmatic advertising, AdTech, digital advertising, campaign management, or publisher operations. Familiarity with the programmatic advertising ecosystem, including technologies such as Google Ad Manager, SSPs, DSPs, or ad exchanges. Comfortable working with advertising performance data, reports, and dashboards. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Excellent communication skills and the ability to explain technical concepts clearly. Proactive, organized, and comfortable working in a fast-paced environment. Interest in working directly with publishers and developing long-term business relationships. Nice to Have Experience with Google Ad Manager or other advertising platforms. Knowledge of header bidding, Prebid.js, or publisher monetization strategies. Previous experience working with publishers, media owners, or advertising technology companies. Experience in campaign optimization, yield management, or programmatic trading. Previous client-facing or Account Management experience. Previous Account Management experience is NOT required. Who Should Apply? We encourage applications from professionals currently working in roles such as: Programmatic Advertising Specialist Programmatic Trader Ad Operations Specialist Campaign Manager (Programmatic) Publisher Operations Specialist Yield Optimization Specialist Digital Advertising Specialist Technical Account Specialist (AdTech) If you have a technical understanding of digital advertising and want to develop your career in publisher relationship management, we'd love to hear from you. Why Join Refinery89? Work at a growing international AdTech company with Dutch roots. Develop expertise in publisher monetization and programmatic advertising. Transition into a more strategic, client-facing position while building on your existing technical knowledge. Collaborate with experienced AdTech professionals across multiple departments. Gain exposure to premium publishers and advanced advertising technologies. Build your career in a dynamic and rapidly evolving industry. Interview Process Our recruitment process consists of four stages: Initial Screening: Introductory call with our Talent Acquisition team. First Interview: Video interview with members of the Publisher Success team. Second Interview: Interview with the Hiring Manager and/or senior stakeholders. Final Interview: In-person meeting with the Hiring Manager and key team members (location to be confirmed). Ready to Take the Next Step? Whether you're currently managing advertising campaigns, optimizing programmatic performance, or supporting publisher monetization, this could be your opportunity to take on greater responsibility and develop your career in AdTech. Apply today and join Refinery89's Publisher Success team in Amsterdam. Find Jobs in Netherlands on Arbeitnow

title: Director, Business Development - Defence & Government (France)
description: Wanna join the adventure? Loft Orbital is hiring a Director, Business Development – Defence & Government to own and grow our relationships and commercial opportunities across the French Ministry of Armed Forces and broader defence and government ecosystem. This is a senior, hands-on role focused on building relationships with key government and military stakeholders, advancing existing opportunities, and developing new business across French defence programmes. You'll take ownership of Loft's engagements with organizations including the DGA , Ministry of Armed Forces and CNES , while also contributing to broader European and international defence, government, and strategic commercial opportunities. The ideal candidate brings deep knowledge of the French defence landscape, whether from a career in the military or government, or from working with these customers within the defence and aerospace industry. While France will be the primary focus, the role offers exposure to a broader range of government and commercial opportunities across Loft. Space experience is valuable, but understanding how to navigate the French government and defence ecosystem is essential. About the Role: Own the full sales cycle with French defence and government customers — from lead generation and qualification through proposal, negotiation and close. Build and deepen relationships across the Ministère des Armées, DGA , Commandement de l'Espace, Agence de l'innovation de défense (AID), CNES and the French prime contractors and integrators that serve them. Win through French public procurement; navigate tenders, innovation programmes and direct contracting routes, and position Loft early so requirements are shaped before formal calls are issued. Lead written and verbal proposals in French and English, translating mission requirements ( ISR , space domain awareness, communications, in-orbit demonstration, science, etc.) into a commercial offer that wins. Negotiate contracts with confidence, handling pricing, terms, security and sovereignty requirements, and deal structure without losing momentum. Identify and contribute to opportunities beyond the core French portfolio, including European defence programmes, allied government customers, and broader strategic partnerships where relevant. Stay close to accounts once programmes are underway, supporting customers and identifying additional opportunities as they emerge. Bring market intelligence back into the business — French and European defence and space priorities, budget cycles, competitor moves and where the market is heading. Must Haves: 5+ years of direct sales or business development experience selling complex technical products or solutions to French defence or government customers, ideally within aerospace, defence, space, or other deep-tech industries. An established network across the French defence and government ecosystem, particularly Minarm and DGA , with familiarity with organizations such as CDE and CNES and an understanding of how French defence programmes are planned, funded and procured. Proven track record of independently developing strategic opportunities, leading complex commercial negotiations, and securing significant institutional or government contracts. Technical understanding of defence, aerospace, intelligence or space systems, including the ability to engage with engineering stakeholders, understand system architectures and capabilities, and translate complex technical concepts into customer value. Excellent communication and executive presence, with the ability to represent an organization credibly in front of senior government, military, and industry leaders. Native or fully professional French and English, written and spoken. Eligible to obtain and hold a French national defence security clearance (habilitation). Nice to Haves: Experience selling mission- or satellite-as-a-service offerings to defence or institutional customers. Strong technical fluency in space hardware and systems — payload integration, spacecraft bus architecture, mission design — enough to earn credibility with engineers and programme officers. Direct experience at a French prime, a scaleup/startup in the space industry, the DGA , CNES or within the French armed forces. Familiarity with European defence funding instruments (e.g. the European Defence Fund) and ESA programmes, and with selling to other European MoDs or international government customers A background in engineering (electrical, mechanical, systems or payload integration) that transitioned into a sales career — hands-on hardware exposure paired with a proven sales track record is ideal. An interest in learning about everything and anything — our job is to make a customer's mission a reality, no matter what it is. Residence in or willingness to relocate to Toulouse, where much of Loft’s France team is located. Paris-based candidates will also be considered. Some of Our Awesome Benefits: Equity, we want you to have an active role in our success Up to 35 days of Paid Time Off (vacations & RTT ) and flexible working hours, we want you to be at your best Health and life insurance, we care about your health Lunch Vouchers, because let’s be honest, we love food! title: Engineering Manager - Realtime
description: ABOUT SUPABASE Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth. ABOUT THE ROLE We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead the Realtime team at Supabase. Realtime lets developers send low-latency messages between clients, track and synchronize user state, and listen to database changes. Those three features are Broadcast, Presence and Postgres Changes. Broadcast also sends from the database and over HTTP, and clients can replay recent messages. Realtime is a globally distributed Elixir cluster built on Phoenix. The team balances low latency, fair limits between projects, and the cost of running the service. Customers expect connections to stay up, so reliability matters as much as new features. The Engineering Manager is a people, delivery and technical role. We don't expect you to write production code, but you you will lead a team of experienced engineers. title: Principal Growth Marketing Strategist
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps.
