title: Academic Dean for MiaPrep Online Academy of Ohio
description: Location : 100% remote (Ohio residency required) Classification : Full-time, exempt Reports to : School Leader Pay Range : $40.00 - $48.00 per hour Welcome to Miaplaza! Our vision is to elevate online learning by applying the most successful approaches in virtual education to create an accessible and inclusive homeschool curriculum platform where all students can be successful! MiaPrep Online Academy of Ohio is our newest offering for Ohio families looking for a flexible public school option. The school will serve grades 7-11 in its first year. The school aims to serve 250 students year one, with plans to grow to over 1,000 students by 2030. ð Role Summary The Academic Dean leads the instructional team and is the school's authority on academic standards at MiaPrep Online Academy of Ohio (MOAO), including student conduct, attendance compliance, and academic integrity. This person is the primary leader for teacher supervision and development, oversees academic data and testing coordination, and works closely with the Student Support team (counselors and advisors), who lead student interventions and support. As a member of the MOAO leadership team, the Academic Dean contributes to schoolwide strategy and helps keep instruction, student culture, and compliance with Ohio requirements working together. The role calls for someone who can coach teachers with warmth and rigor, handle sensitive student and family situations with sound judgment, and use data to make decisions. CORE RESPONSIBILITIES Instructional Staff Management Directly supervise instructional staff, holding weekly 1:1s focused on coaching, support, and goal setting. Lead recruiting, onboarding, and training for new teachers. Observe live instruction and office hours on a bi-weekly basis and provide actionable feedback. Monitor grading practices to ensure students receive timely, high-quality feedback. Complete annual and semi-annual walk-throughs and performance reviews as outlined by the ODEW and manage bi-weekly timecard approvals. Coordinate instructional and grading coverage for teacher absences. Address performance concerns through clear expectations, documentation, and, when needed, formal improvement plans in partnership with People Operations. Student Conduct, Attendance & Academic Integrity Own the school's student conduct process, from initial report through investigation, determination, and documentation, applying policy consistently and fairly and creating policy where needed. Oversee academic integrity cases, including investigating suspected plagiarism, AI misuse, and other violations, and ensuring consistent, well-documented outcomes. Own the school's truancy and attendance compliance process, including required notifications, documentation, and filings under Ohio law. Partner with the Student Support team, which leads outreach, intervention plans, and ongoing student support. Hand off cases and coordinate so that accountability and support work together. Serve as the escalation point for teachers and Student Support on conduct, attendance, and integrity concerns. Communicate with students and families about conduct and integrity decisions in a way that is clear, respectful, and focused on getting students back on track. Maintain accurate records and report on trends in conduct, attendance, and integrity cases to school leadership.Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Keep handbooks, policies, and procedures current in these areas. Academic Data & Testing Coordination Analyze course-, teacher-, and school-level data on performance, engagement, and attendance to identify trends, risks, and opportunities. Turn data into action by recommending and implementing instructional strategies, and share insights with Student Support to inform their interventions. Serve as the school's testing coordinator for Ohio state assessments and other required or school-administered testing, including scheduling, proctoring logistics, test security, accommodations coordination, and make-up testing. Partner with the appropriate teams on state data reporting, ensuring accuracy and timeliness. Prepare clear summaries of academic and testing data for leadership, teachers, and families. Professional Development Design and lead regular PD sessions for instructional staff, informed by teacher feedback, observation, and student data. Build a culture of continuous improvement, reflective practice, and growth for the instructional team. Collaborate with school and company leadership on schoolwide professional learning priorities. Curriculum & Cross-Team Collaboration Serve as the primary point of contact between the instructional team and the Content team on curriculum, checkpoint assignments, and MiaPrep platform issues. Gather teacher and student feedback and make curriculum recommendations. Support consistency in instructional practice and expectations across courses and departments. Lead regular instructional team meetings to align resources, expectations, and practices. Assist teachers in comparing their curriculum to the OST blueprints to identify gaps, and create a plan to fill these gaps in the short and long term.Â What We're Looking For Proven leadership experience managing, coaching, or mentoring teachers Sound judgment and a steady hand with sensitive student, family, and staff situations; knows when to resolve and when to escalate A collaborative approach to working across teams, especially with student support professionals Excellent written and verbal communication, including documentation that holds up to scrutiny A fair, consistent, relationship-first approach to discipline and accountability Comfort with data and the ability to translate it into clear decisions Exceptional organization and follow-through across many concurrent priorities Resilient, adaptable, and committed to continuous improvement in a fast-paced environment Growth mindset with a focus on coaching and constructive feedback THIS POSITION IS FOR A CURRENT VACANCY, AND THE EMPLOYER INTENDS TO FILL THIS POSITION BY DECEMBER 1ST, 2026. Requirements: Bachelor's degree required; master's degree in education, educational leadership, or a related field preferred Valid Ohio teaching license and/or administrator license, or ability to obtain one, to be confirmed against current requirements At least 3 years of teaching experience At least 2 years of experience in a leadership role such as department chair, instructional coach, dean, or assistant principal Experience in virtual school settings or teaching online Experience supervising employees and conducting evaluations or performance reviews Comfort working in online learning environments and with learning management and student information systems The Ideal Candidate Brings: Experience administering or coordinating standardized testing and working with student assessment data Experience as a member of a founding team for a new school Compensation & Benefits The expected starting pay range is $40.00 - $48.00 per hour. An Academic Dean at MiaPrep Online Academy of Ohio works an average of 40 hours per week. When working year-round, this can equate to an annual pay range of $83,000 - $99,800. Miaplazaâs compensation philosophy ensures equity and competitiveness while considering the regional differences in living and labor costs. Specific rates will be provided during the hiring process and are aligned with market data and internal equity. Compensation is evaluated twice per year, based on performance. Full-time employees are eligible for health, dental, and vision insurance, inclusive of specialty care options like fertility benefits, mental health services, and chiropractic care, FSA, HSA, and more. All employees are eligible for a retirement plan with employer match. PTO is all-purpose time off, and combines traditional vacation and paid sick leave plans into one flexible, inclusive policy. Eligible employees can use PTO for all kinds of absences including: vacation, holidays, illness, injury, family leave, and other personal business. Full-time employees receive 16 hours of floating holiday PTO per quarter and accumulate additional PTO at the rate of 1 hour per every 15 hours worked. Annually, this amounts to approximately 200hours per year or 25 eight-hour days on average. Parental leave, and other perks and benefits are also available. We invite your family and friends to join our journey! All employees receive free site memberships and discounted MOHS tuition for the children in their household, plus two additional memberships for other children in their lives. â¡ï¸ You can hear our CEO, Johannes Ziegler, discuss our companyâs values and future here ! â¡ï¸ Learn more by visiting our careers page ! We consider all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, sex, orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, age, or arrest/conviction records in accordance with applicable laws. We'll work with you to provide any necessary adjustments, including alternate versions of the assessment or assignment based on your needs. title: Product Engineering Lead
description: Join Tether and Shape the Future of Digital Finance At Tether, weâre not just building products, weâre pioneering a global financial revolution. Our cutting-edge solutions empower businessesâfrom exchanges and wallets to payment processors and ATMsâto seamlessly integrate reserve-backed tokens across blockchains. By harnessing the power of blockchain technology, Tether enables you to store, send, and receive digital tokens instantly, securely, and globally, all at a fraction of the cost. Transparency is the bedrock of everything we do, ensuring trust in every transaction. Innovate with Tether Tether Finance: Our innovative product suite features the worldâs most trusted stablecoin, USDT , relied upon by hundreds of millions worldwide, alongside pioneering digital asset tokenization services. But thatâs just the beginning: Tether Power: Driving sustainable growth, our energy solutions optimize excess power for Bitcoin mining using eco-friendly practices in state-of-the-art, geo-diverse facilities. Tether Data: Fueling breakthroughs in AI and peer-to-peer technology, we reduce infrastructure costs and enhance global communications with cutting-edge solutions like KEET , our flagship app that redefines secure and private data sharing. Tether Education : Democratizing access to top-tier digital learning, we empower individuals to thrive in the digital and gig economies, driving global growth and opportunity. Tether Evolution : At the intersection of technology and human potential, we are pushing the boundaries of what is possible, crafting a future where innovation and human capabilities merge in powerful, unprecedented ways. Why Join Us? Our team is a global talent powerhouse, working remotely from every corner of the world. If youâre passionate about making a mark in the fintech space, this is your opportunity to collaborate with some of the brightest minds, pushing boundaries and setting new standards. Weâve grown fast, stayed lean, and secured our place as a leader in the industry. If you have excellent English communication skills and are ready to contribute to the most innovative platform on the planet, Tether is the place for you. Are you ready to be part of the future? About the job QV.AC is a general purpose AI assistant that runs locally on your devices. It gives people real control over their data and how they use AI. No cloud dependency, no data harvesting, and no one else's servers between you and your assistant. Our focus is local, on-device, privacy-preserving AI, connected across Tether's peer-to-peer ecosystem. We're building the AI assistant people actually own. Product sets the direction. We're looking for a Product Engineering Lead to turn that direction into features people love, built to a standard that holds up on real devices with real constraints. You lead the teams that build QV.AC's features and app experience on top of our local AI stack, each with its own lead. You report directly to the CTO and take direction from product. Product owns the what and the why. You own the how and the engineering bar. The split is roughly 70% engineering leadership and 30% product. You're a combination of three things. You're an engineering leader who has helped teams ship consumer products at speed. You have real product sense and can partner with PMs as an equal, shaping what gets built, not just executing it. And you have an intuition for AI systems and their limits, so you can turn emerging capabilities into features that work reliably on-device, without needing to build the models yourself. Responsibilities Engineering - Run the app and feature teams day to day: unblocking, reviewing, and keeping them shipping.- Set and hold a high engineering bar for performance, reliability, and clean APIs.- Own the technical design of features and the API surface between our AI core and the app.- Make sure your teams work closely with our AI research and deep tech teams on code reviews, design, and anything that touches models or inference. Product Partnership - Work alongside QV.AC's product managers to turn vision and roadmap into scoped, buildable work.- Push back when scope and reality don't match, and propose better paths when they exist.- Bring an engineering perspective to product decisions, especially on what local models can do well today and what they can't yet.- Help the team move fast, using AI tools and quick prototypes to validate ideas before committing to them. Leadership - Create clarity around team goals and make sure everyone knows what success looks like.- Mentor team leads to build strong team operating systems, improve how their teams work with others, and grow as leaders.- Lead by example: roll up your sleeves when the team needs it, and step back when they're ready to own it. Mandatory: Experience managing engineers or engineering leads who ship consumer product, ideally AI-powered apps. Strong product sense : you can tell a good feature from a busy one. Intuition for applied AI and on-device constraints : model size, latency, memory, battery, and the gap between a good demo and a reliable feature. You don't need ML research expertise, because our core abstracts it away. You use AI tools heavily in your own work and enjoy experimenting with new models and capabilities. Deep JavaScript and React . Initiative, curiosity, resilience , and the ability to give and receive direct critique. Preferred: Bonus: Experience with local or on-device inference, LLM evals, cross-platform mobile and desktop apps, or open source . title: Global Demo Engineer
description: WHO WE ARE Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vkpYpWfEK5s. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion. Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work. ABOUT THE ROLE: As one of Notion’s founding Demo Engineers, you’ll build the global demo engine behind how we bring Notion’s most important customer stories to life. You’ll shape the standards, systems, and experiences that help our Sales teams demonstrate what is possible with Notion, from the first customer conversation through implementation and deployment. This is a high-impact opportunity to create the function from the ground up. You’ll establish global standards, turn our strongest customer solutions into repeatable demos, and give regional teams the tools and autonomy to innovate. Your work will directly influence how customers understand Notion’s platform, AI capabilities, and potential to transform how their organizations work. This role reports to the Global Head of Acquisition and partners closely with Sales, Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE), Enablement, and PMM. This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days. WHAT YOU'LL ACHIEVE: - Build the global demo engine that brings Notion’s most important customer stories to life - Partner with Enablement and PMM to define the core narratives, scripts, environments, and assets for each demo - Create a durable release and versioning process so demos stay current as the product evolves - Automate repeatable setup and maintenance wherever possible so the system can scale globally - Turn Notion’s strongest customer and internal solutions into reusable GTM assets - Identify high-impact use cases and transform them into repeatable, field-ready demos - Partner with FDE to package customer solutions, implementation guidance, and technical patterns into demos the field can confidently deliver - Work with GTM Systems to translate demos into workspaces that can be deployed in customer environments - Set the global standard for demo quality and help the field deliver it - Define what great looks like for each demo moment, from the first customer conversation to a tailored technical experience - Train and coach customer-facing teams on storytelling, environment setup, delivery, and troubleshooting - Partner with Enablement to create practical resources and programs that raise demo quality across regions - Create a clear path from experimentation to global scale - Give customer-facing teams a structured way to safely build, test, and pilot new demo concepts - Evaluate the strongest ideas and turn them into scalable standards, templates, and reusable assets - Serve as the strategic demo partner for high-impact opportunities - Advise teams on custom or personalized demos that fall outside the standard portfolio - Help teams balance customer relevance, technical credibility, and speed without compromising quality SKILLS YOU'LL NEED TO BRING: - 5+ years in a technical or customer-facing role such as Solutions Engineering, Sales Engineering, Demo Engineering, Solutions Architecture, or Software Engineering - Experience designing and delivering technical demos, prototypes, or solution experiences for a SaaS product - Strong systems thinking, with experience building scalable standards, templates, documentation, versioning practices, and operating processes - Ability to translate complex product capabilities into clear, compelling customer stories tied to business value - Technical fluency across APIs, integrations, automation, data, permissions, and enterprise security concepts - Working proficiency with scripting or automation tools such as Python or JavaScript - Experience partnering across Sales, Product, Engineering, Enablement, and Marketing to drive alignment and deliver shared outcomes - Strong communication and coaching skills, with the ability to raise the capabilities of customer-facing teams - Comfort creating structure, setting priorities, and making progress in a fast-moving environment with evolving requirements NICE TO HAVES: - Experience building or scaling a demo engineering, solutions engineering, or technical enablement function - Experience with enterprise sales cycles and complex, multi-stakeholder customer environments - Hands-on experience with demo automation platforms such as Consensus, Navattic, Reprise, Storylane, or Demostack - Experience supporting major product launches or global go-to-market programs - Familiarity with AI coding tools such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor - Experience with productivity, collaboration, AI, or horizontal SaaS products - Notion power user TOOLS YOU'LL USE: - Demo environments: Notion, plus demo automation platforms as needed - Collaboration: Slack, Salesforce, Gong for call review - Automation: Zapier, scripting tools, API clients (Postman or similar) - AI Coding Tools: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Notion is committed to providing highly competitive cash compensation, equity, and benefits. The compensation offered for this role will be based on multiple factors such as location, the role’s scope and complexity, and the candidate’s experience and expertise, and may vary from the range provided below. For roles based in San Francisco or New York City, the estimated range for total on target earnings (including base salary and on target incentive pay) for this role is $220,000 - $250,000 per year. title: Platform Engineer, Managed Postgres
description: ABOUT SUPABASE Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth. ABOUT THE ROLE We are seeking a Platform Software Engineer with deep experience in distributed systems to help design, build, and maintain core platform services. You will work primarily in TypeScript and Go to deliver reliable, scalable, and secure systems that power Supabase at massive scale. WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING: - Design and implement distributed services and APIs that power the Supabase Platform. - Lead projects that improve scalability, reliability, and cost efficiency across existing systems. - Build data-intensive workflows, background jobs, and event-driven pipelines. - Own service SLIs/SLOs and collaborate on incident response and post-incident reviews. - Improve system observability with metrics, logging, tracing, and profiling. - Contribute to our CI/CD and release processes to ship safely and quickly. - Partner with product teams to deliver features end-to-end, from design docs to production. - Write clear design documents, RFCs, and high-quality tests. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR: - Experienced in designing and operating distributed systems, with strong foundations in consistency, fault tolerance, partitioning, consensus, and back pressure. - Proficient in TypeScript and/or Go, ideally with 5+ years building production services in one or both languages (other languages also considered). - Comfortable with cloud infrastructure (AWS preferred) and container orchestration. - Familiar with multi-tenant architectures, API design, and data modelling. - Knowledgeable about networking fundamentals and security best practices. - Experienced with Infrastructure as Code (Pulumi preferred; Terraform/CDK also fine). - Comfortable participating in on-call rotations for large-scale production systems. NICE TO HAVE: - Experience with Postgres internals, logical replication, or CDC pipelines. - Experience with service meshes, workload identity, or zero-trust networking. - Background in performance engineering and capacity planning. - Open source contributions in systems, databases, or runtime tooling. WHAT WE OFFER - Fully Remote We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world. - ESOP Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together. - Tech Allowance Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work. - Health Benefits Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us. - Annual Off-Sites Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year. - Flexible Work We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when. - Professional Development Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth. ABOUT THE TEAM Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love. - ~400 team members - 60+ countries - 20+ languages spoken - Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F) - 540,000+ community members We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

title: Senior Site Reliability / Gitops Engineer
description: <p>Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.</p> <p>The company is founder-led, profitable, and growing.</p> <p>We are hiring a <strong>Senior Site Reliability / Gitops Engineer</strong> to our Information Systems (IS) team. <span style="font-weight: 400;">This role is an opportunity for an “automation-first” senior technologist</span><span style="font-weight: 400;"> with a passion for Linux to build a career with Canonical and drive the success with those leveraging Ubuntu and open source products.  If you have experience of IT operations automation, Infrastructure as Code and a passion for technology, then you will enjoy working with some of the best people in the industry at Canonical.</span></p> <h2><strong>Job Summary</strong></h2> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">The IS team at Canonical supports and maintains all of Canonical’s IT production services. title: Cloud Platform Engineer
description: ABOUT THE ROLE As a Cloud Platform Engineer at Supabase, you’ll join Cloud Engineering, part of Engineering Operations, and shape the foundations that let engineering teams build, ship, and operate infrastructure safely and independently across AWS and GCP. This is a role spanning cloud governance, platform engineering, and hands-on operations. You’ll work across AWS and GCP account structure, identity and access management, Infrastructure as Code (IaC), reusable platform primitives, security boundaries, and self-service workflows for engineers. You’ll be joining at a point where many of these foundations are being actively defined or reworked. We’re looking for someone who can take ambiguous, messy, business-critical infrastructure problems and turn them into pragmatic systems, tools, standards, and written guidance that scale with the company and empower teams to go faster. WHAT YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR - Designing and implementing cloud governance across AWS and GCP, including identity, account organization, access controls, and guardrails. - Building reusable infrastructure and building blocks using Infrastructure as Code (IaC), enabling teams to provision and manage infrastructure safely and consistently. - Creating self-service capabilities that reduce organizational friction and let engineers move more quickly within sensible boundaries. - Owning resource governance and visibility: management tagging, a trustworthy inventory of what exists and who owns it, and consistent cross-account billing data. - Developing reusable security primitives, including secrets storage, KMS, certificate management, token vending, direct service-to-service authentication, mTLS, and related platform services. - Owning cloud-level network and operational primitives: IP address management, DNS, and health signals such as service-limit and quota alerting. - Combining software engineering with hands-on operations and total ownership: building, deploying, monitoring, troubleshooting, and improving what you own. - Establishing and sharing cloud engineering best practices through documentation, internal tooling, examples, and enablement. YOU MIGHT BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU - Have 5+ years of experience in cloud governance, platform engineering, and/or operations, have operated production systems at scale, and carried on-call for them. - Have previously undertaken a significant migration, e.g. rearchitected an AWS account topology, introduced IaC for existing infrastructure, centralized identity/SSO, or brought a second cloud under governance. - Enjoy building internal platform and self-service experiences for other engineers. - Are genuinely deep in at least one—ideally two—of the three strength areas below (and tell us which is your center of gravity): - Tooling & ecosystem: You’re intimately familiar with the breadth of AWS services in general, and IAM/SSO in particular. You know their Well-Architected Framework, and when to reach outside. You have working knowledge of GCP. You use IaC routinely and have run it in production, whichever tool. You’ve probably collaborated with auditors on meeting compliance requirements. - Software engineering: You write real production code (Go, Rust, or a comparable systems language), and can build reliable, maintainable services. You thrive across all stages of the SDLC, set technical direction, know how to de-risk projects, and produce written artifacts such as RFCs. - Operations: You’ve run production infrastructure yourself: carried the pager, written the alerts and runbooks, used SLOs or similar to decide what to fix first, and made shared systems less risky over time. You like owning systems, simplifying complex infrastructure problems, and turning best practices into reusable building blocks. - Are comfortable treating infrastructure as software and have relevant experience with IaC and automation. - Communicate clearly, work with a wide range of stakeholders, and thrive in async, globally distributed teams. - Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and iterating toward better systems over time. WHAT WE OFFER - Fully Remote We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world. - ESOP Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together. - Tech Allowance Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work. - Health Benefits Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us. - Annual Off-Sites Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year. - Flexible Work We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when. - Professional Development Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth. ABOUT THE TEAM Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love. - ~400 team members - 60+ countries - 20+ languages spoken - Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F) - 540,000+ community members We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

title: Talent Sourcer
description: WHO WE ARE Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vkpYpWfEK5s. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion. Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work. ABOUT THE ROLE: We're looking to hire a new Talent Sourcer in Tokyo to build top-of-funnel talent pipelines and shape talent strategy across our Go-To-Market (GTM) organization. In this role, you'll partner with regional leadership to fill critical GTM roles like Solutions Consultants https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/notion/15dde0f5-b3fd-4d46-8ec2-0858ebdd888d and Outcomes Architects https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/notion/7030916f-4277-45db-9fed-644bb3fba059 primarily in Japan. WHAT YOU'LL DO: - You'll manage the sourcing process from inception through successful close, ensuring an exceptional experience for candidates and hiring managers at every step - You'll serve as a strategic advisor and talent sourcing expert, leading successful searches across GTM roles - You'll conduct initial qualification screenings and casual chats with candidates to assess fit and build relationships - You'll collaborate with the broader team on process improvements, programs, and strategic initiatives - You'll lead talent branding initiatives, including organizing hiring webinars and publishing blogs and articles that feature our employees - You'll provide talent mapping and market insights to support local and global recruiting and hiring teams - You'll make informed data-driven decisions that build efficiencies into the sourcing process - You'll find creative and unconventional ways to help us build a diverse top-of-funnel for GTM roles across all levels - You'll help build and manage partnerships to bring more underrepresented talent to Notion - You'll advance our Inclusion, Diversity, Equity, and Accessibility (I.D.E.A) strategy, working to build more diverse and inclusive teams WHAT YOU'LL ACHIEVE: - Manage sourcing for multiple complex and evergreen searches, creating innovative strategies and engagement to bring the best and most diverse talent to Notion - Help develop and execute comprehensive sourcing plans, analyzing role requirements to define target profiles and identify qualified candidates - Partner closely with other members of the Recruiting team to ensure we hit our hiring targets without sacrificing quality - Collaborate closely with Hiring Managers throughout the recruiting process to ensure we meet their hiring needs and goals - Establish and maintain meaningful relationships with management and key cross-functional stakeholders SKILLS AND TOOLSET YOU'LL NEED TO BRING: - At least 3 years of experience in talent sourcing or recruitment, whether in-house or agency, or relevant transferable skills from related fields - Experience using LinkedIn Recruiter and other sourcing tools, with skills in Boolean and AI-powered searches (or eagerness to learn these tools) - Persistence, consistency, and attention to detail - if we hire one person out of 200 candidates, you'd ensure the other 199 have a great experience. You care deeply about your craft. - Strong time management, prioritization, and organizational skills. You are self-motivated and committed to excellence - You are kind, warm, and thoughtful - you'll represent the company when you interact with thousands of candidates each year - You'll contribute across the full scope of recruiting operations, from maintaining our ATS database and finding new ways to source candidates to analyzing data to improve recruiting efficiency and managing sourcing channels - Fluency in Japanese and business-level English A NOTE ON AI You don’t need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect every Notino to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement — when that’s the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don’t treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on. EQUAL OPPORTUNITY & ACCOMMODATIONS We hire talented people from a wide range of backgrounds. If you’re excited about this role but don’t meet every bullet, we still encourage you to apply. Notion is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any legally protected characteristic. Consistent with applicable law, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. Notion provides reasonable accommodations during the application process; if you need one, please let your recruiter know. Notion is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate in hiring or any employment decision based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, genetic information, veteran status, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. Notion considers qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Notion is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please let your recruiter know.

title: Ubuntu Linux Kernel Engineer - Silicon Enablement
description: <p>Ubuntu Linux is already the most popular Linux distribution in the world, and its mission is to remain at the forefront of the global software ecosystem. As the industry evolves, we are expanding our support for a wider array of System on Chip (SoC) platforms to ensure that every user receives a high-performance and reliable experience. There is growing and vital demand from major silicon manufacturers such as NVIDIA, AMD, Qualcomm, MediaTek, and Renesas to provide Ubuntu Linux as the foundational platform for their next-generation hardware.</p> <p>The Canonical Kernel Team is responsible for the build, maintenance, and distribution of the Linux kernel for Ubuntu. We are looking for engineers who share our passion for building high-quality, robust software foundations that others can rely upon. This role sits at a critical junction in the software stack, ensuring that the underlying hardware is seamlessly integrated, optimized and prepared to meet the demands of modern computing.</p> <p>While direct experience with the Linux kernel would be an advantage, it is not a hard requirement. Candidates with RTOS or bare-metal experience and demonstrable hardware experience are encouraged to apply.</p> <p>We welcome applications from engineers at various stages of their careers, from those beginning their journey in hardware-level development to seasoned industry veterans.</p> <h2><strong>Location</strong></h2> <p>This is a globally remote role.</p> <h2><strong>What the role entails</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Drive the integration of platform support from our silicon partners into the Ubuntu Linux kernel</li> <li>Lead the identification and resolution of complex kernel issues reported by partners, customers, or discovered through rigorous testing</li> <li>Own the delivery of distinct, silicon-optimized variants of the Ubuntu Linux kernel to the global community</li> <li>Develop and refine the tooling and automation required for the reliable delivery and testing of our kernels</li> <li>Manage the submission and review process for upstream patches, collaborating effectively with both internal and external maintainers</li> <li>Identify new methodologies and strategies for maximizing performance on partner silicon</li> <li>Collaborate proactively within a globally distributed engineering team to ensure cohesive outcomes across the organization</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What we are looking for in you</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Proficiency in C programming, particularly for low-level system development</li> <li>A strong grasp of device drivers, BSPs, and other aspects of hardware-level system engineering</li> <li>Deep understanding of operating system kernel fundamentals</li> <li>Professional proficiency with Git for version control and collaborative development</li> <li>Ability to communicate effectively in English, both written and verbal, within description: <p>Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.</p> <p>The company is founder led, profitable and growing.</p> <p>We are hiring <strong>2025 and 2026 Graduate Software Engineers</strong> into engineering teams around the world. As a global platform company we offer a wide range of software engineering challenges, in both open source products and commercial business systems. We have teams that work in a variety of languages, typically Python, Golang, Rust, C/C++, JavaScript and of course... Bash. We work from the very lowest levels of the Linux system - BIOS and boot loaders, firmware, kernel and drivers, all the way up to desktop applications and containers. We work on tiny devices like the Raspberry Pi and new RISC-V boards, all the way up to supercomputers, clouds and Kubernetes clusters. We work on compilers and toolchains, and we work on security, cryptography, performance and documentation. Some of our teams focus on packaging thousands of pieces of software, others focus on deep contributions to a single body of code.</p> <p>If you are excited about the potential that open source has for humanity and the enterprise, you have outstanding results in your academic career, and you are excited to contribute to the open source stack, this is the best way to apply to Canonical. challenging and exciting start to your career.</p> <p><strong>Location: </strong>This is a Globally remote role.</p> <h3>The role entails</h3> <ul> <li>Shaping the roadmap for your product at global Golang, JavaScript or Java</li> <li>Experience with Ubuntu or another Linux distribution</li> <li>Track record of going above-and-beyond expectations to achieve outstanding results</li> English</li> <li>Excellent interpersonal skills, curiosity, flexibility, and accountability</li> <li>Personal responsibility and accountability</li> <li>Thoughtfulness, self-awareness and the ability to reflect and develop</li> <li>Ability to travel internationally twice a year for company events up to two weeks long</li> </ul> <h3>Nice-to-have skills</h3> <ul> <li>Upstream open source contributions</li> <li>Packaging and Linux distribution contributions - Debian, Fedora, Arch, Nix or another</li> <li>Leadership and organization skills</li> <li>Presentation and writing skills</li> <li>Business and commercial interests</li> </ul> <h3>What we offer colleagues</h3> <p>We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. title: Head of AI Native Operations
description: ABOUT SUPABASE Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth. About the Role We are looking for a Head of AI Native Operations to build the autonomous systems that run Supabase. Supabase is building an AI-native internal operating system, where agents carry the operational load end to end. We are standing up a new central team to build that platform and run it in production. This is the role that leads it, and it is hands-on. You design the architecture, build the first versions of the critical pieces, and are accountable for whether every agent we run is correct, safe, and improving over time. We build rather than buy, and there are no settled best practices for most of this yet, so you will be setting them. You will lead a team of senior individual contributors extending the platform and driving adoption across teams. What You’ll Be Responsible For In this role, you’ll: - Own the agent platform architecture: The harness and orchestration layer and connectors into company systems, shared context and memory, and the path from prototype to production. - Catch regressions before they ship: Model, prompt, and tool changes can’t ship until they pass the evals. When a new model comes out, you know within hours whether to adopt it. - Make every agent observable: Every run and every decision is traced. For any agent at any time, you can answer what it did, why, what it cost, and how its quality is trending. - Own safety and trust: Design the controls that let agents act without a human in the loop: least-privilege credentials, hard policy limits, escalation thresholds, audit logs, sandboxing, and prompt-injection defenses. - Replace workflows, don’t assist them: Pick the workflows agents can fully own today and take them to production. - Turn wins into a platform: Package what works into reusable components, templates, and eval harnesses so other teams can ship their own production agents without starting from scratch. - Build and direct the team: Hire and grow senior ICs, review their designs and pull requests, and hold the quality bar. - Measure what matters: Track workflows automated, eval pass rates, cost per run, and work absorbed against the hiring plan. How You’ll Think A Point of View on Where Automation Wins You have a thesis about how AI and automation change the way a company operates, and it comes from building, not reading. You can look at a business and say which workflows agents can own today, which they will own in 12 months as models improve, and which still need people, and why. You defend that view with evidence from systems you have shipped, and you update it when the evals tell you to. Eval-Driven You don’t trust an agent because the demo looked good. You trust it because it passes a test set of real cases, and you know which cases it fails. When anything changes, your first question is “what do the evals say?” Inversion Thinking Left alone, an autonomous system tends to fail quietly, or people route around it. So the first question about any agent isn’t “does it work on the happy path?” but “how will this break, and how will we know?” The design follows from that answer: what the agent is never allowed to do, what it escalates, and which alert fires when quality drifts. Recursive Thinking Every system you build should produce the evidence that grades it. An agent isn’t done when it works. It’s done when it tells you, without you in the loop, that it has stopped working. Must Have - Hands-on agent building: Have personally designed and built autonomous agent or LLM systems that ran in production and that others depended on. Prototypes, demos, and configuring a vendor tool don’t count. You don’t need to be a career software engineer, but you must have built these systems yourself. - Architecture depth: Can explain how the pieces fit together (orchestration, tool and data access, context and memory, tracing, evals, guardrails, deployment), with opinions on current frameworks. - Security judgment: Have shipped agents that take real actions with real permissions, and designed the controls that made that safe. - A tested point of view: Can argue, with examples from your own builds, where autonomous systems create real business leverage and where they don’t yet. - Technical leadership: Have led senior builders and set the quality bar through design and code review. Strong Signal - Have replaced a human-run business workflow (finance, operations, support, release management) end to end with an autonomous system. - Are native to Git, Markdown, and pull requests, and comfortable reading and writing Python or TypeScript. - Have taken an internal platform from zero to adoption by teams you did not control. - A software engineering background is a plus, but not required. What Success Looks Like - Six months: 20+ autonomous agents in production on the shared platform, each with an eval suite, tracing, and a named owner. - Regressions get caught, not discovered: Quality problems surface in an alert or dashboard before a user reports them. - Workflows replaced, not assisted: Multiple high-volume workflows are fully owned by agents, with humans handling only escalations. - Trusted by default: No agent causes material financial, security, or customer harm, and every agent’s permissions and actions can be audited. - Teams ship their own: At least three teams outside the core team run production agents built on the platform. - Autonomous team: Your two reports work independently, and you spend your time on architecture and review rather than execution. WHAT WE OFFER - Fully Remote We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world. - ESOP Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together. - Tech Allowance Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work. - Health Benefits Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us. - Annual Off-Sites Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year. - Flexible Work We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when. - Professional Development Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth. ABOUT THE TEAM Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love. - ~400 team members - 60+ countries - 20+ languages spoken - Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F) - 540,000+ community members We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

counsel inside a listed company.</li> <li>A technical or engineering background, or fluency in how software is built and shipped.</li> <li>Experience of a subscription or recurring-revenue business From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work. ABOUT THE ROLE Notion is building the operating system for knowledge work, and we want people to be able to do substantive knowledge work from their phone. A great native app is what makes that possible. On Android, that means Notion should feel like it was built for the platform: fast to open, smooth to scroll, and reliable offline or on a spotty connection. We’re investing in a more native foundation for how people read, write, and edit in Notion. That lets users capture ideas in the moment, find answers across their workspace, manage tasks and projects, and work with teammates, with the speed, polish, and dependability people expect from the best apps on their phone. As an Android engineer, you’ll help build that native foundation, from how pages render and how people write and edit, to the navigation and app chrome people use every day, like Home, Search, and Inbox, along with the shared frameworks the rest of the app is built on. You’ll work across the Android stack, with chances to dig into our shared Rust layer and the AI tools we use for mobile development. Along the way, you’ll pair with experienced product and mobile AI engineers to find what slows the team down, try new Android capabilities, and help decide what ships in the app. This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days. WHAT YOU'LL ACHIEVE - Ship the core Notion experience on Android: Build and polish the surfaces people use every day—opening and reading pages, writing and editing, navigating the app, and the Home, Search, and Inbox tabs—on a native Kotlin and Jetpack Compose stack that is fast to open, smooth to scroll, and dependable offline. - Build with product and design, and iterate fast: Partner with product managers and designers to turn ideas into shipped features, then use feedback and data to make them better. Use AI coding tools and agents to build, test, and investigate faster, while you stay accountable for review, validation, and quality. - By the end of your first year, own a core product area: Take a core part of the Android app, like Home, Inbox, or a piece of the editor, from idea to launch, and shape it into an experience that helps people do their life’s work from their phone. - Make the app feel fast and reliable: Find and fix issues in startup time, scrolling, typing latency, crashes, and memory use across the surfaces you own, and add the tests and monitoring that catch regressions before users do. SKILLS YOU'LL NEED TO BRING - Solid Android fundamentals: You’ve built and shipped Android apps, through work, internships, or your own projects, and you’re comfortable with modern Android—Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Coroutines/Flow, and Gradle. Experience with a large, modular codebase is a plus. - Care for native UI and performance: You enjoy making UI feel fast and smooth, and you’re curious about things like custom text rendering, complex lazy lists, or rich-text editing. Experience with performance profiling, realtime collaboration, or offline sync is a plus. - Product instincts: You care about how the app feels to use, not just how it works. You sweat the details of interactions and polish, and you use feedback and data to decide what to build next. - Thoughtful problem-solving and clear communication: You build a clear picture of the problem before jumping to a fix, you can explain trade-offs in writing, and you ask for help early when you’re stuck. Experience moving a hybrid or web-based surface to native, or building something from 0→1, is a plus. - AI-native, end-to-end engineering practice: You use AI tools and agents as real collaborators, framing tasks clearly, reviewing generated changes, testing behavior, and designing workflows that make the broader team more effective. Web experience (TypeScript, React, Node) is welcome but not required. Notion is committed to providing highly competitive cash compensation, equity, and benefits. title: Partner Sales Director - IHV Alliances
description: <p>Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.</p> <p>The company is founder-led, profitable, and growing.</p> <p>We are seeking a highly motivated and experienced <strong>IHV Alliance Sales Director</strong> to join our strategic partnerships team who will be responsible for leading IHV Alliances globally, in AMER, EMEA or APAC regions. Reporting to the Head of IHV Alliances, the IHV Alliance Sales Director will work closely with IHV and Canonical teams in those geographies to develop and maintain strong relationships with senior executives at strategic partner organizations, fostering collaboration and alignment on joint business objectives. The IHV Alliance Sales Director will manage and grow a team of Business Development Managers and help them identify and pursue new business opportunities with IHVs, driving revenue growth and market expansion, develop and execute go-to-market strategies for joint offerings, oversee the day-to-day management of alliances including contract negotiations and performance tracking, and issue resolution. </p> <p>The Director is responsible for building trusted relationships with IHV partners, increasing Canonical market share and attach rate, evangelising the partnership and leading all business interactions from engineer to CxO. They will often run customer workshops focused on particular initiatives at that customer, attend sales events, give public presentations and lead executive engagements.</p> <p>Location: This role will be based remotely in AMER, EMEA or APAC regions.</p> <p><strong>As an IHV Alliance Sales Director you will:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Build strategic relationships with IHV partners at all levels</li> <li>Grow their awareness of open source capabilities on Canonical Ubuntu</li> <li>Demonstrate a deep understanding of the Linux and cloud software ecosystem</li> <li>Negotiate contracts and commercial business terms</li> <li>Demonstrate a deep understanding of large and complex organizations</li> <li>Lead partnerships in APAC with companies like Lenovo, Huawei, Quanta, Fujitsu, Inspur, H3C,  NEC, Asus etc.</li> <li>Lead partnerships in EMEA with companies like Ericsson, Nokia, Bull, Siemens</li> <li>Lead partnerships in the Americas with companies like Dell, HPE, IBM, Supermicro</li> <li>Work closely with marketing, sales engineering and product management</li> <li>Deliver on targets, objectives and provide a voice of the partner</li> <li>Lead executive interlocks between IHV and Canonical leadership</li> <li>Travel regularly - sometimes internationally - to drive partnerships in person</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>Valued skills and experience</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience in alliance or indirect sales management roles</li> <li>Autonomous, disciplined, hands-on, get-it-done mentality</li> <li>Ability to capture customer requirements, evaluate gaps, identify and create opportunities</li> <li>Passionate about Ubuntu products and mission</li> <li>Comfortable in fast-paced and high pressure environments with measurable goals</li> <li>Experience with Linux, virtualization, containers, and other cloud technologies.</li> <li>Excellent communication and presentation skills</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>What we offer colleagues</strong></p> <p>We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognize outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.</p> <ul> <li>Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person</li> <li>Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year</li> <li>Annual compensation review</li> <li>Recognition rewards</li> <li>Annual holiday leave</li> <li>Maternity and paternity leave</li> <li>Team Member Assistance Program & Wellness Platform</li> <li>Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues</li> <li>Priority Pass and travel upgrades for long-haul company events</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>About Canonical</strong></p> <p>Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open-source projects and the platform for AI, IoT, and the cloud, we are changing the world of software. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence; in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Most colleagues at Canonical have worked from home since our inception in 2004.​ Working here is a step into the future and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.</p> <p> </p> <p><strong>Canonical is an equal opportunity employer</strong></p> <p>We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products.<a href="https://canonical.com/careers/diversity/identity"> Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.</a></p> <p>#LI-remote</p>

title: Technical Product Manager AI Stockbroking App
description: About KIRA Our mission is to make money smart, reliable and within reach for everyone. Â In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia. Â Today, we are expanding ways to help people in Asia and it includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and at ease and self reliance, become an expert. We believe AI will help us achieve this in our generation. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future. If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you. The Role KIRA is building a AI Stockbroking Superapp for Southeast Asia across payments, remittance, insurance, wealth, and trading. Â These products move real money. Reliability, regulatory requirements, and third-party financial rails are fundamental to the product - not considerations around the edges. Â The Technical Product Manager owns a product vertical end-to-end , from strategy and outcomes through technical design, delivery, and launch. Â We are AI-native by default, but AI is a means, not the goal. The bar is knowing where AI genuinely improves an outcome, where deterministic systems must remain in control, and how to build products that are reliable, auditable, and trusted. Â What You'll Own Owning a product vertical end-to-end, including strategy, metrics, roadmap, priorities and delivery. Shaping technical design with engineering across APIs, data flows, ledgering, reconciliation, failure handling, security and scalability. Driving trade-offs across correctness, speed, cost, reliability, regulatory requirements and user experience. Building regulatory requirements into the product across KYC, transaction monitoring, limits, privacy and licensing. Applying AI where it improves outcomes, with clear evaluation, safeguards, human oversight and failure handling. Shipping products around external dependencies, including regulatory approvals, financial rails and third-party partners. Aligning Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance around clear product decisions and launch requirements. Â What We're Looking For 5+ years of product management experience, including ownership of complex technical products from strategy through production. Strong technical foundation across system architecture, APIs, databases, workflows, failure modes and distributed systems. Experience working closely with engineers and ability to review, challenge and contribute to technical designs. Experience in payments, banking, remittance, insurance, trading or another regulated, high-consequence product domain. Strong product judgment and ability to make difficult trade-offs under technical, regulatory and operational constraints. Experience building with LLMs or AI products, including evaluation, reliability and understanding when AI should not be used. Â Nice to have Engineering or highly technical product background. Experience building zero-to-one fintech or consumer products. Experience defining evaluation frameworks for ML or LLM-powered products. Â Outcome Clear vertical strategy and legible roadmap Ships fast and clears the gates that actually block launch Money is correct and users are never misled about the state of their funds AI features are valuable, predictable and trusted Trade-offs made deliberately under uncertainty and hold up when challenged Engineering, design, compliance, and operations are aligned with minimal friction Location This is a remote role . We hire globally and work across multiple countries and time zones. Candidates should be comfortable working effectively in a distributed, fast-moving international team and collaborating with colleagues across different locations. Language English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required. title: Engineering Manager - App Stores
description: <p>Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.</p> <p>The company is founder-led, profitable, and growing.</p> <p>This is a technical management role to lead a team that develops Python and Golang micro-services that power our global software distribution engine. The world sees it as the <a href="https://snapcraft.io/store">Snap Store</a> and <a href="https://charmhub.io/">Charmhub.io</a> marketplaces, behind the scenes it is a unified system that understands key concepts in software distribution - architectures, releases, betas, release candidates, stable releases, branches and more. We are on a journey to transform the experience that people all over the world have with their open source software by significantly expanding the range of software we can deliver through this system. If you have a passion for clean APIs, believe that great engineers ship software calmly and regularly against an agile plan, and know that tests are the key to higher velocity and reliability, you'll fit right in.</p> <p>This is a great opportunity to take part in engineering a highly scalable SaaS product (think about the load on our systems when one of our largest Ubuntu Desktop snaps is updated by the publisher, for instance). In addition, you will have the opportunity to learn from Canonical's world-class security team as we work collectively to deliver this capability, safely, to our customers around the world.</p> <p>As an Engineering Manager at Canonical, you must be technically strong, but your main responsibility is to run an effective team and develop the colleagues you manage. You will develop and review code as a leader, but know that the best way to improve the product is to ensure that the whole team is focused, productive and unblocked. You are expected to help them grow as engineers, do meaningful work, do it outstandingly well, find professional and personal satisfaction, and work well with colleagues and the community. You will also be expected to be a positive influence on culture, facilitate technical delivery, and regularly reflect with your team on strategy and execution. You will collaborate closely with other Engineering Managers, product managers, and architects, producing an engineering roadmap with ambitious and achievable goals.</p> <p>We expect Engineering Managers to be fluent in the programming language, architecture, and components that their team uses. Code reviews and architectural leadership are part of the job. The commitment to healthy engineering practices, documentation, quality and performance optimisation is as important, as is the requirement for fair and clear management, and the obligation to ensure a high-performing team.</p> <p>This is a great opportunity to really learn how to do engineering of a highly-scalable SaaS product (think about the load on our systems when one of our largest Ubuntu Desktop snaps is updated by the publisher, for instance).  In addition, you will have the opportunity to learn from Canonical's world-class security team as we work collectively to deliver this capability, safely, to our customers around the world.</p> <p><strong>Location</strong>: This role may be based remotely in the Americas, Europe, Middle East or Africa time zones.</p> <h3>What your day will look like</h3> <ul> <li>Lead a remote team of engineers in your time zone</li> <li>Develop talent through coaching, mentoring, feedback, and hands-on career development</li> <li>Set and manage expectations with other engineering teams, management, and external stakeholders</li> <li>Be an active part of the leadership team and collaborate with other leaders in the organisation</li> <li>With your team, build clean web service APIs to support both CLI and web frontend clients, using Python (and optionally Golang).</li> <li>Engage with many other teams at Canonical, as well as the open-source community and commercial partners</li> </ul> <h3>What we are looking for in you</h3> <ul> <li>Good experience in leading modern, agile software development practices</li> <li>Experience in forming a healthy, collaborative engineering culture in line with the company values</li> <li>Demonstrative experience of being a role model for sound engineering principles and directly contributing toward your team's goals</li> <li>Willingness to travel up to 4 times a year for internal events</li> <li>You love to mentor, develop and grow people, and have a track record of doing it</li> <li>You are knowledgeable and passionate about software development</li> <li>You are focused on success and the timely delivery of high-quality software</li> <li>You value and nurture great team culture and spirit</li> <li>You have experience and commitment to agile development methodologies</li> <li>Software development experience in Python (experience in Golang in addition to that would be a big plus)</li> <li>Effective written and verbal communication skills</li> <li>Practical experience with Linux system administration</li> </ul> <h3>What we offer you</h3> <p>Your base pay will depend on various factors including your geographical location, level of experience, knowledge and skills. In addition to the benefits above, certain roles are also eligible for additional benefits and rewards including annual bonuses and sales incentives based on revenue or utilisation. Our compensation philosophy is to ensure equity right across our global workforce.</p> <p>In addition to a competitive base pay, we provide all team members with additional benefits, which reflect our values and ideals. Please note that additional benefits may apply depending on the work location and, for more information on these, you can ask in the later stages of the recruitment process.</p> <ul> <li>Fully remote working environment - we’ve been working remotely since 2004!</li> <li>Personal learning and development budget of 2,000USD per annum</li> <li>Annual compensation review</li> <li>Recognition rewards</li> <li>Annual holiday leave</li> <li>Parental leave</li> <li>Employee Assistance Programme</li> <li>Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues at ‘sprints’</li> <li>Priority Pass for travel and travel upgrades for long haul company events</li> </ul> <h3>About Canonical</h3> <p>Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open-source projects and the platform for AI, IoT, and the cloud, we are changing the world of software. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence; in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Most colleagues at Canonical have worked from home since our inception in 2004.​ Working here is a step into the future and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.</p> <h4>Canonical is an equal opportunity employer</h4> <p>We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products.<a href="https://canonical.com/careers/diversity/identity"><span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span>Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.</a></p> <p>#LI-remote </p>

Analysis, agents, and automated pipelines that surface segments, generate offer candidates, and run campaigns with minimal manual work Design and ship targeted offers for specific segments and moments: reload bonuses, lossback, wager bounties, challenges, win-back sequences. Email, in-app, Telegram, whatever the channel. You're hands-on with it, with AI doing the heavy lifting Partner with engineering and design to ship the product surfaces that make all of this repeatable What we're looking for Strong intuition for player psychology and incentive design. Experience in gambling, gaming, fintech, or consumer marketplaces helps. Genuine curiosity about why people behave the way they do is required Deeply analytical. You can go from a vague question to a clean cohort cut yourself, without waiting on a data scientist AI-native by default.
